為你已經走到的這裡，我替你驕傲。
對你即將前往的遠方，我替你有信心。

但最想跟你說的是：
別急著趕路，
記得抬頭看看沿途的風景。

終點會等你，
但風景不會。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫在畢業卡片、或當致詞的溫暖收尾，把「肯定過去、祝福未來、珍惜當下」三層意思疊在一起，不落俗套又有重量
variations: 驕傲你走過的，期待你要去的，也捨不得你錯過現在的。
願你有奔向遠方的勇氣，也有停下來看風景的從容。

en.content:
I'm proud of how far you've already come.
I have faith in the distance you're about to go.

But what I most want to say is this:
don't rush the road —
remember to look up at the view along the way.

The finish line will wait for you.
The scenery won't.
en.editorNote: Ideal for a graduation card or the warm close of a speech — it layers pride in the past, faith in the future, and a nudge to savor the present, without slipping into cliché
variations: Proud of where you've been, excited for where you're headed, and rooting for you to notice where you are.
May you have the courage to chase the horizon, and the ease to stop and enjoy the view.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自畢業帽標語「I did it for the WiFi / Thanks Mom & Dad's wallet」，改寫成中文畢業帽金句組合

zh-tw.content:
畢業帽上寫什麼，決定了你是哪種人：

「我是為了WiFi才來的。」
「感謝爸媽的錢包。」
「終於可以合法睡到自然醒。」
「學貸：故事未完待續。」

選一句，戴上去，畢業快樂。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給正在煩惱畢業帽要寫什麼的人一份靈感清單，每句都能直接抄；貼IG當畢業帽DIY靈感也很好用
variations: 畢業帽的字數有限，但你的厭世可以無限。
帽子上寫什麼不重要，重要的是你真的畢業了（可能吧）。

en.content:
What you write on your grad cap says everything:

"I only came for the WiFi."
"Thanks, Mom & Dad's wallet."
"Finally legal to sleep in."
"Student loans: to be continued."

Pick one, wear it proudly, happy graduation.
en.editorNote: A ready-to-steal idea list for anyone stuck on what to put on their grad cap — great as Instagram inspiration for DIY cap decorating too
variations: Your grad cap has a word limit. Your existential dread does not.
Doesn't matter what the cap says. What matters is you actually graduated (probably).

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「輕輕的我們相聚一起，無限歡聲笑語；輕輕的我們又要分離」畢業離別語，改寫為現代口語版

zh-tw.content:
我們是輕輕地相遇的。

一起笑、一起熬夜、一起在群組裡吵著要不要翹課。
然後有一天，
也要輕輕地分開了。

沒有轟轟烈烈，
但那些一起浪費過的時間，
後來都變成了最捨不得的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業季傳給朝夕相處的同學或室友，或搭配合照貼IG；用「輕輕」這個詞把離別寫得溫柔，不煽情卻很戳心
variations: 我們沒有轟轟烈烈的告別，只有一句「那……先這樣囉」，然後各自走進不一樣的人生。
最珍貴的從來不是那些大事，是我們一起浪費掉的每一個平凡下午。

en.content:
We came together quietly.

Laughed together, pulled all-nighters together,
argued in the group chat about whether to skip class.
And then one day,
we'll part just as quietly.

Nothing dramatic.
But all that time we wasted together
became the thing we can't bear to let go of.
en.editorNote: For the classmates or roommates you saw every single day — send it at graduation or pair it with a group photo; the softness of a quiet goodbye lands harder than anything loud
variations: We never had a dramatic goodbye — just a 'well… guess this is it,' and then two different lives.
The most precious things were never the big moments. They were the ordinary afternoons we wasted together.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「感謝Google、維基百科、複製貼上」與「全世界最貴的一張紙」畢業笑話，重新創作合併

zh-tw.content:
畢業感言：

感謝Google、維基百科、ChatGPT，
還有發明「複製、貼上」的那位偉人。

沒有你們，就沒有這張
全世界最貴的一張紙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼IG畢業照或當畢業帽文案都很好用，比正經的感謝詞更好笑也更真實；特別適合理工科或熬夜趕報告過來的人
variations: 我要感謝在我不相信自己的時候，唯一相信我的——咖啡因。
四年的努力，換來一張紙和一屁股的學貸，超值。

en.content:
Graduation acknowledgments:

Thank you Google, Wikipedia, ChatGPT,
and whoever invented copy & paste.

Without you, there'd be no
most expensive piece of paper in the world.
en.editorNote: Perfect as an Instagram caption or grad cap line — funnier and more honest than a real thank-you speech, especially for anyone who survived on last-minute assignments
variations: Special thanks to caffeine, for believing in me when I didn't believe in myself.
Four years of work traded for one piece of paper and a mountain of debt. Worth it.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「我畢業了，代表我很會假裝自己知道在幹嘛」與「求職DM我」畢業笑話，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
我畢業了。

這代表我正式取得了
「假裝自己知道在幹嘛」的專業認證。

各位老闆，
履歷我準備好了，
工作offer請直接私訊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛畢業、正在找工作的人貼IG或發限動，把求職的焦慮包裝成幽默；配上西裝或畢業照特別有反差感
variations: 畢業證書：一張證明你很會考試、但不保證你會做人的紙。
現在的我：非常驕傲，非常累，非常需要一份工作。

en.content:
I graduated.

Which officially certifies me as
a professional at pretending I know what I'm doing.

Dear employers,
resume's ready.
DM me your job offers.
en.editorNote: For the fresh grad in the middle of a job hunt — turn the anxiety into a joke on Instagram or your story; pairs perfectly with a suit or cap-and-gown photo
variations: A diploma: proof you're good at taking tests, no guarantee you're good at anything else.
Current status: very proud, very tired, very much in need of a job.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「你的教育是地基，不是天花板」勵志語，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
你學到的這些，
是地基，不是天花板。

它不是用來限制你能蓋多高，
是用來撐住你之後想蓋的一切。

畢業不是蓋好了，
是終於可以開始蓋了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫在畢業卡片上送給學弟妹或好友，也很適合當畢業致詞的收尾；把「畢業」重新定義成起點而非終點，鼓勵人不要被學歷框住
variations: 文憑證明你學過什麼，不決定你能成為什麼。
畢業那天不是你人生的高峰，只是你終於準備好去爬更高的山。

en.content:
Everything you learned here
is a foundation, not a ceiling.

It's not there to cap how high you can go —
it's there to hold up everything you build next.

Graduation isn't the finished building.
It's finally being ready to start building.
en.editorNote: Great for a card to a younger friend or classmate, or as the closing line of a graduation speech — it reframes the diploma as a starting point and reminds people not to let a degree define their limits
variations: A diploma proves what you studied. It doesn't decide what you become.
Graduation day isn't the peak of your life. It's just the day you're finally ready to climb a bigger mountain.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自 Yogi Berra「如果你不知道要去哪，最後可能會到別的地方」，重新創作為給迷茫者的溫柔語錄

zh-tw.content:
畢業時還不知道自己要去哪，
沒關係。

有人一畢業就有清楚的路，
有人是走著走著才慢慢看清楚。

你不用現在就有答案，
你只需要，先往前走一步。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給那些畢業後還很迷茫、看著同學都有規劃而焦慮的人；不催不逼，只是溫柔地告訴他們「還沒想清楚」也是可以的
variations: 路是走出來的，不是想出來的。先動起來，方向會慢慢清楚。
沒有計畫不代表沒有未來，只是你的故事還沒寫到那一頁。

en.content:
You graduate and still don't know where you're going?
That's okay.

Some people leave with a clear road ahead.
Some only see it clearly after they start walking.

You don't need the answer right now.
You just need to take one step forward.
en.editorNote: For the grad who feels lost while everyone else seems to have a plan — no pressure, just a gentle reminder that not having it figured out yet is completely fine
variations: A path gets made by walking it, not by thinking about it. Start moving, and the direction gets clearer.
No plan doesn't mean no future. Your story just hasn't reached that page yet.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「慶祝結束，因為它們是新開始的前奏」，重新創作為畢業感人語錄

zh-tw.content:
會捨不得，是因為真的很好。

那些一起排隊的午餐、
考前互相安慰的訊息、
下課後不想回家的散步——

它們不會再回來了，
但正因為結束，
才證明我們真的擁有過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業季搭配合照貼IG，或傳給一起走過這段路的人；用「捨不得代表擁有過」這個角度，把離別的難過轉成溫暖的感謝
variations: 謝謝你們，讓「畢業」這兩個字這麼難說出口。
有些時光之所以珍貴，正是因為它有結束的一天。

en.content:
It hurts to leave because it was truly good.

The lunch lines we waited in together,
the pre-exam texts talking each other off the ledge,
the walks after class when nobody wanted to go home —

they won't come back.
But it's the ending itself
that proves we really had them.
en.editorNote: Pair it with a group photo on Instagram, or send it to the people you went through it all with — it turns the sadness of goodbye into gratitude by framing the ache as proof you truly had something
variations: Thank you all for making the word 'graduation' this hard to say.
Some moments are precious precisely because they were always going to end.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「他們說我可以成為任何人，所以我變得很累」，重新創作為畢業搞笑語錄

zh-tw.content:
從小大家都說：
你長大想當什麼都可以。

於是我認真思考了四年，
最後決定——
先當一個很想睡覺的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在畢業照或限動，戳中每個「明明可以成為任何人、卻只想躺平」的畢業生；短、好笑、超好轉發
variations: 他們說天空才是極限，但我看了一下我的存款，決定先以天花板為目標。
小時候的夢想是成為大人，現在夢想是回去當小孩，這算完成夢想又反悔嗎？

en.content:
Growing up, everyone told me:
you can be anything you want.

So I thought hard about it for four years,
and finally decided —
to be someone who really wants a nap.
en.editorNote: Perfect for a grad photo or story; it nails every graduate who could 'be anything' but mostly wants to lie down — short, funny, and endlessly shareable
variations: They said the sky's the limit, but I checked my bank balance and set my sights on the ceiling for now.
As a kid I dreamed of becoming an adult. Now I dream of going back to being a kid. Does that count as achieving the dream and then filing a refund?

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自 C.S. Lewis「前方有遠比我們身後更美好的事物」，重新創作為畢業勵志語錄

zh-tw.content:
你會捨不得現在擁有的，
這很正常。

但請相信一件事：
你身後那些最好的日子，
其實還沒有身前的多。

最好的，不是回憶，
是還沒發生的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給站在畢業路口、又期待又害怕的人；不否定過去的美好，而是溫柔地把眼光轉向前方，讓離別多一點盼望
variations: 回頭看很美，但別看太久，因為好戲還在前面。
畢業不是把最好的留在後面，而是走去領還沒拆封的那些。

en.content:
It's normal to not want to let go
of what you have right now.

But believe this one thing:
the best days behind you
are fewer than the ones still ahead.

The best part isn't the memory —
it's what hasn't happened yet.
en.editorNote: For anyone standing at the graduation crossroads, equal parts excited and scared — it honors the past without clinging to it, gently turning the gaze forward so the goodbye carries some hope
variations: Looking back is beautiful, but don't stare too long — the good part is still ahead.
Graduation isn't leaving the best behind. It's walking off to collect the parts you haven't unwrapped yet.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自畢業帽短語「終於畢業了 / 我為了WiFi撐下來的」，重新創作為畢業搞笑語錄

zh-tw.content:
有人問我，
是什麼撐著你念完這幾年？

是夢想嗎？
是熱情嗎？

不，是圖書館的免費冷氣
跟不用錢的網路。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業帽 slogan 或限動短句，把「其實沒那麼偉大」的真心話講出來，越誠實越好笑
variations: 撐我走到畢業的三大支柱：咖啡因、期末報告的死線、還有絕對不能被當的恐懼。
問我大學學到什麼？學到圖書館幾點關、哪間便利商店的微波爐最快。

en.content:
Someone asked me,
what kept you going all these years?

Was it a dream?
Was it passion?

Nah. It was the library's free AC
and the Wi-Fi I didn't have to pay for.
en.editorNote: Ideal for a grad cap slogan or a short story caption — say the unglamorous truth out loud; the more honest it is, the funnier it lands
variations: The three pillars that carried me to graduation: caffeine, final-paper deadlines, and the pure fear of failing.
Ask me what I learned in college? What time the library closes and which convenience store has the fastest microwave.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「畢業是慶祝新開始」的新起點主題，重新創作為畢業感人語錄

zh-tw.content:
畢業那天，
你不會突然變成另一個人。

你還是會迷路、還是會害怕、
還是那個半夜想很多的你。

改變的只是，
從今天起，
你要開始牽著自己的手往前走了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給即將離開校園、對「長大」感到不安的人；不畫大餅，只是承認害怕、再輕輕推他一把，比空泛的加油更有力量
variations: 沒有人畢業那天就準備好了，我們都是邊走邊變勇敢的。
以前有人替你撐傘，以後你要學會自己淋雨，也自己找屋簷——這就是長大。

en.content:
On graduation day,
you won't suddenly become someone else.

You'll still get lost, still get scared,
still be the you who overthinks at 3 a.m.

The only thing that changes is:
from today on,
you start holding your own hand and walking forward.
en.editorNote: For the one about to leave campus and feeling uneasy about 'growing up' — no grand promises, just admitting the fear and giving a gentle push, which lands harder than an empty 'you got this'
variations: Nobody is actually ready on graduation day. We all get braver as we go.
Someone used to hold the umbrella for you. Now you learn to take the rain and find your own shelter — that's what growing up is.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「感謝 Google 和 Quizlet 讓我拿到學位」的自嘲式畢業梗，重新創作為台灣版搞笑語錄

zh-tw.content:
得獎感言：

感謝我的家人、感謝我的教授，
以及最重要的——
感謝那位每次都把共筆傳給我的同學。

這張證書有一半是你的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業照 IG 貼文，也很適合 tag 那個救你無數次的組員；自嘲又帶點感謝，比純吐槽更討喜
variations: 四年的成果，濃縮成一張紙、一頂帽子，和三十七個未讀的課程公告。
我不是拿到學位，我是通關了。

en.content:
Acceptance speech:

Thank you to my family, thank you to my professors,
and most importantly —
thank you to the classmate who shared their notes every single time.

Half of this diploma is yours.
en.editorNote: Great for a grad photo caption, and even better for tagging the group-project teammate who carried you — self-deprecating but warm, which lands better than pure snark
variations: Four years, condensed into one piece of paper, one hat, and thirty-seven unread course announcements.
I didn't earn a degree. I beat the game.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「The tassel was worth the hassle」等雙關短句，重新創作為中英文各自成立的短句版本

zh-tw.content:
熬的夜、補的考、重修的學分，
最後都變成今天帽子上那條穗。

值了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 字數短、節奏乾脆，適合當 IG 限動或畢業照的一句話配文；也可以只留最後兩個字
variations: 四年、八學期、無數個「明天再說」——結案。
我的青春有點狼狽，但結局還不錯。

en.content:
The late nights, the retakes, the credits I had to do twice —
they all turned into this one tassel.

Worth it.
en.editorNote: Short and punchy, built for a Story or a single-line photo caption; you can also post just the last two words
variations: Four years, eight semesters, countless 'I'll do it tomorrow' — case closed.
My college years were a mess, but the ending holds up.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「Graduated. Unemployed. Optimistic.」的求職現實梗，重新創作為台灣求職情境版

zh-tw.content:
目前狀態：

已畢業。
無業。
心情很好。

三選二我覺得已經很棒了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 畢業後那段還沒找到工作的空檔最適合發；把焦慮講成笑話，比硬撐「一切順利」真實得多
variations: 履歷投了四十封，回覆兩封，其中一封是「已收到您的履歷」。
從被當掉的恐懼，畢業到被已讀不回的恐懼。

en.content:
Current status:

Graduated.
Unemployed.
Weirdly upbeat.

Two out of three feels like a solid score.
en.editorNote: Perfect for that post-grad gap before the first offer — turning the anxiety into a joke reads truer than pretending everything's on track
variations: Sent forty applications. Got two replies. One was an auto-confirmation.
I've graduated from fear of failing a class to fear of being left on read by recruiters.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「青春不散場，我們不說再見，只說再會」的告別主題，重新創作為感人語錄

zh-tw.content:
我們不說再見。

因為再見是給那些
以後不會再見的人。

我們說的是——
下次換你請客。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫在畢業卡片或傳給死黨；把離別的重量用一句玩笑接住，反而更催淚
variations: 散場不代表結束，只代表下一場我們要各自買票進去。
以後我們不再同一間教室，但約在同一間店，這件事一直都算數。

en.content:
We're not saying goodbye.

Goodbye is for people
you won't see again.

What we're saying is —
next round's on you.
en.editorNote: For a graduation card or a message to your closest friends; catching the weight of goodbye with a joke somehow hits harder
variations: The show ending just means we buy our own tickets to the next one.
We won't share a classroom anymore, but that standing invitation to our usual spot never expired.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「畢業不是終點，而是旅程的起點」的新起點主題，重新創作為勵志語錄

zh-tw.content:
以前有課表，
有學分，有及格線，
有人告訴你今年要修完什麼。

以後沒有了。

可怕的是沒有了，
自由的也是沒有了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送給對「畢業之後怎麼辦」感到茫然的人；點出恐懼和自由其實是同一件事，比單純喊加油更能安慰人
variations: 學校教你怎麼考試，出社會才開始教你怎麼選擇。
沒有人再幫你排課表了，這聽起來很慌，但也表示這次你自己排。

en.content:
There used to be a schedule,
credits, a passing grade,
someone telling you what to finish this year.

Now there isn't.

The scary part is that there isn't.
So is the free part.
en.editorNote: For anyone lost about what comes after graduation — naming fear and freedom as the same thing comforts more than a generic 'you got this'
variations: School taught you how to take tests. Real life starts teaching you how to choose.
Nobody's building your schedule anymore. Terrifying — and it means this one's yours to write.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自畢業後身分轉為校友、母校開始募款的現實觀察，重新創作為搞笑語錄

zh-tw.content:
畢業那天最神奇的事，
不是拿到證書。

是學校從此不再管你上不上課，
卻開始每年寄信，
問你要不要捐款。

原來我不是畢業，
是被升級成提款機。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合收到母校募款信時發限動，或丟到系上群組引起共鳴；把「校友」這個新身分的荒謬講出來，比單純抱怨學費更好笑
variations: 在學的時候他們追著你交作業，畢業之後他們追著你交錢，唯一沒變的是都在追你。
母校的愛很長久，長久到你畢業十年還會準時收到它的匯款帳號。

en.content:
The weirdest part of graduation day
wasn't getting the diploma.

It's that the school suddenly stopped caring
whether I showed up to class,
and started emailing every year
asking for donations.

Turns out I didn't graduate.
I got upgraded to an ATM.
en.editorNote: Perfect for a story when your alma mater's fundraising email lands, or for the group chat — naming the absurd new 'alumni' identity beats complaining about tuition
variations: In school they chased you for assignments. After graduation they chase you for money. The only constant is being chased.
Your alma mater's love runs deep — deep enough that ten years out, it still has your bank details.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自畢業時承諾每年辦同學會、實際卻逐年遞減的主題，重新創作為感人偏搞笑語錄

zh-tw.content:
畢業的時候大家都說：
「我們每年都要辦同學會！」

第一年來了三十個，
第二年來了八個，
第三年剩下三個人，
在群組裡互相問
「所以到底還要不要辦」。

沒關係，那三個是真的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那幾個不管過多久還是會出現的老同學；先笑同學會的消散，再收在「留下來的才是真的」，暖得剛剛好
variations: 同學會的人數會逐年遞減，但會出現的永遠是同一批人，那批人就別搞丟了。
承諾每年見面的有一百個，真的每年見面的有三個，人生大概就是這樣篩出來的。

en.content:
At graduation everyone swore:
'We'll do a reunion every single year!'

Year one, thirty showed up.
Year two, eight.
Year three, three of us
asking in the group chat
if we're even still doing this.

That's okay. Those three are real.
en.editorNote: Send it to the handful who still show up no matter how much time passes — laughing at the fading reunion first, then landing on 'the ones who stay are the real ones,' warm without the sap
variations: Reunion turnout drops every year, but it's always the same people. Don't lose them.
A hundred promised to meet up yearly. Three actually do. That's pretty much how life filters.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自「大四天涯何處有芳草」的校園青春老哏，重新創作並收在學貸的現代結局

zh-tw.content:
大一的時候覺得自己是一株嫩草，
大二覺得自己開始開花，
大三發現花快謝了，
大四站在畢業典禮上，
低頭一看——

草都沒了，只剩學貸還在長。
zh-tw.editorNote: 改寫自那首「大四天涯何處有芳草」的老哏，收在學貸這個現代版結局，適合畢業季發文自嘲
variations: 四年前我是校園裡最青春的一片草皮，四年後我是履歷上最需要澆水的那一格。
念了四年，青春沒了，長出來的是每個月的待繳明細。

en.content:
Freshman year, you feel like a fresh green sprout.
Sophomore year, you start to bloom.
Junior year, the flowers are already wilting.
Senior year, standing at the ceremony,
you look down and —

no grass left. Just student loans, still growing.
en.editorNote: A modern spin on the old 'four years of youth' verse, landing on the student-loan punchline — good for a self-deprecating graduation post
variations: Four years ago I was the freshest patch of grass on campus. Now I'm the line on my résumé that needs the most watering.
Four years in: the youth is gone, and the only thing that grew is the balance due.

items.sourceNote: 靈感來自畢業典禮拋帽瞬間的真實觀察，重新創作為搞笑語錄

zh-tw.content:
畢業典禮最感人的一刻，
是全場一起把帽子拋向天空。

然後最尷尬的一刻，
是全場一起發現——

沒有人記得自己的帽子長什麼樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配拋帽照發限動；大家都拍那個往上拋的浪漫瞬間，很少人講落下來之後那段兵荒馬亂，反差很好笑
variations: 拋帽的時候我們是一個團體，撿帽的時候我們是一場混戰。
帽子往上拋的那一秒是青春，撿到別人帽子的那一秒是社會的第一課。

en.content:
The most moving moment of graduation
is everyone tossing their caps into the sky together.

The most awkward moment
is everyone realizing, together —

nobody remembers what their own cap looks like.
en.editorNote: Pair it with your cap-toss photo; everyone captures the romantic throw, almost nobody talks about the scramble when they come back down — the contrast is the joke
variations: Tossing the caps, we were one class. Retrieving them, we were a free-for-all.
The second the cap goes up, that's youth. The second you catch someone else's, that's your first lesson in real life.

items.sourceNote: 畢業感人語錄，台灣校園意象，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
鳳凰花開的時候，
沒有人告訴你這是最後一次
一起在樹下等打鐘。

驪歌唱完，蟬還在叫，
只是台下坐的人，
下次見面就要各自訂高鐵票了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配畢業季校園空景或鳳凰花照片發限動；用台灣人熟悉的鳳凰花、驪歌、蟬聲堆疊離別感，比直接說「捨不得」更有畫面
variations: 蟬聲一年比一年吵，但能一起在樹下聽的人，一年比一年少。
驪歌不是唱給學校聽的，是唱給那個以後不會再天天見面的我們聽的。

en.content:
When the flame trees bloom,
nobody tells you it's the last time
you'll wait under them for the bell together.

The farewell song ends, the cicadas keep going,
but the people in the seats below
will need to book separate trains to meet again.
en.editorNote: Pair it with an empty-campus or graduation-season photo; it stacks familiar early-summer imagery instead of just saying 'I'll miss you,' which lands with more of a picture
variations: The cicadas get louder every year, but the friends who'll sit under the tree and listen with you get fewer.
The farewell song isn't sung for the school. It's sung for the us that won't be seeing each other every day anymore.

items.sourceNote: 畢業搞笑語錄，論文與指導教授，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
終於畢業了。

這代表我再也不用在半夜兩點
盯著指導教授的已讀不回，
猜他到底是要我大改還是小改。

現在換老闆已讀不回，
但至少這次有薪水。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛口試完或剛入職的研究所朋友；把寫論文等回覆的痛，無縫接軌到職場的痛，苦中作樂的共鳴很強
variations: 論文教會我最重要的一件事：不是研究方法，是等一個人回訊息可以等到懷疑人生。
畢業證書上寫著我的專業，只有我自己知道，我真正練成的是「改到第八版還能微笑」。

en.content:
Finally graduated.

Which means no more staring at 2 a.m.
at my advisor's 'seen' with no reply,
guessing whether it's a full rewrite or a tiny fix.

Now it's my boss leaving me on read —
but at least this time there's a paycheck.
en.editorNote: Send it to a grad-school friend who just defended or just started a job; it links the pain of waiting on thesis feedback straight to office life, and the gallows humor really connects
variations: The most important thing my thesis taught me wasn't methodology. It was that waiting for one reply can make you question your entire existence.
My diploma says my major. Only I know the skill I actually mastered was smiling through the eighth round of revisions.

items.sourceNote: 畢業搞笑勵志語錄，職場現實，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
畢業快樂。

現在開放接受：
工作機會、免費食物、
以及任何形式的人生方向。

薪水可談，夢想面議，
三餐能不能溫飽再說。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛畢業求職中的人發限動或當IG caption；用「開放接受」的清單句式自嘲，比認真喊「加油」更符合現在畢業生的心情
variations: 履歷上寫著「積極主動、抗壓性強」，翻譯成白話就是：拜託給我一份工作，什麼都可以。
以前煩惱的是這學期會不會被當，現在煩惱的是這個月會不會被裁，內容升級，焦慮不變。

en.content:
Happy graduation.

Now accepting:
job offers, free food,
and any form of life direction.

Salary negotiable, dreams TBD,
three meals a day still under review.
en.editorNote: Great for a job-hunting new grad's story or IG caption; the 'now accepting' list format self-deprecates in a way that fits today's grads better than an earnest 'you got this'
variations: My resume says 'proactive, thrives under pressure.' Translation: please, any job, I'll take anything.
I used to worry about failing a class this semester. Now I worry about getting laid off this month. The content got an upgrade; the anxiety stayed the same.

items.sourceNote: 研究生論文自嘲哏，原創

zh-tw.content:
我的畢業論文，終於過了。

這篇嘔心瀝血的鉅作，
全世界大概只有三個讀者：
我、我的指導教授，
還有 Turnitin。

而其中最認真看完的，是最後那位。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫論文寫到懷疑人生的研究生畢業時發，理工商管文組都能會心一笑，也可以tag一起被論文折磨的同學
variations: 花了兩年寫的論文，被引用次數：0。被自己重看的次數：也是0。我們都選擇了向前看。
口試那天教授問我：「這段是你自己寫的嗎？」我愣了三秒才想起來——對，真的是我寫的，只是我也不記得了。

en.content:
My thesis finally passed.

This masterpiece I bled over
has maybe three readers in the entire world:
me, my advisor,
and the plagiarism checker.

And honestly, the checker read it the most carefully.
en.editorNote: Perfect for grad students who spent months on a thesis nobody will ever read; tag the classmates who suffered through it alongside you
variations: Two years writing my thesis. Times it's been cited: zero. Times I've reread it: also zero. We both chose to move on.
At my defense a professor asked, 'Did you write this part yourself?' I froze for three seconds before remembering—yes, I did. I just don't remember doing it.

items.sourceNote: 室友情誼，原創溫情向

zh-tw.content:
大一開學那天，
學校隨機分配了一個陌生人
當我的室友。

四年後我才發現，
那場隨機，
給了我一個自己選的家人。

謝謝那台不知道在想什麼的分配系統。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給即將各奔東西的室友或宿舍死黨，把「緣分是隨機開始的、感情是自己選的」講得剛剛好，貼在合照底下很催淚
variations: 當初系統把我們湊成室友，是巧合。四年來我們沒把對方逼瘋、反而變成一輩子的朋友，這絕對不是巧合。
我們共用過一間房、一台冰箱、還有無數個崩潰的夜晚。畢業後房間要退了，但那個家，我打算一直住下去。

en.content:
On my first day of college,
the school randomly assigned a stranger
to be my roommate.

Four years later I realized
that random draw
handed me a family I actually got to choose.

Thanks to whatever algorithm wasn't really thinking.
en.editorNote: For the roommate or dormmates you're about to scatter across the map; captions a group photo perfectly—friendship that started by chance and stayed on purpose
variations: The system pairing us up was a coincidence. Four years of not driving each other insane and becoming lifelong friends instead—that was not.
We shared one room, one fridge, and countless breakdowns. The room goes back after graduation, but that home? I'm keeping it.

items.sourceNote: 手機相簿自嘲哏，原創

zh-tw.content:
四年大學生活的唯一證據，
不是這張畢業證書，
是我手機裡那三萬張照片：

一半是拍不清楚的上課投影片，
另一半是拍得超清楚的宵夜。

輕重緩急，我分得很清楚。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合愛拍照的人畢業發文，自嘲又真實，配一張亂七八糟的相簿截圖效果最好
variations: 整理手機準備畢業，才發現我幫每一份鹹酥雞都留了影，卻連一張像樣的畢業照都沒有。優先順序清清楚楚。
別人的回憶是青春與夢想，我的回憶是32G的模糊板書和拍到會流口水的食物。各有各的珍貴。

en.content:
The only real proof of my four years of college
isn't this diploma.

It's the 30,000 photos on my phone:
half are blurry lecture slides,
the other half are perfectly focused midnight snacks.

My priorities were always crystal clear.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose camera roll is 90% food; pair it with a screenshot of your chaotic photo library for max effect
variations: Cleaning out my phone for graduation, I found a photo of every plate of fries I ever ate—and not one decent grad photo. Priorities, crystal clear.
Other people's memories are youth and dreams. Mine are 32GB of blurry whiteboards and food shots so sharp they make you drool. Both precious, in their way.

items.sourceNote: 綽號回憶哏，原創苦甜向

zh-tw.content:
出社會以後，
再也沒有人會叫你那個綽號了。

那個只有大學同學才懂、
由某件蠢事命名的稱號，
以後只會在同學會上被翻出來一次，
然後大家笑到流淚。

所以趁現在，多叫幾聲吧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合有一群互相取綽號的死黨畢業時發，勾起那種「只有我們懂」的默契，tag那群人保證被已讀狂敲
variations: 以後的同事只會叫你的全名，只有這群人記得，你曾經因為一件蠢事，被冠上一個丟臉到現在還會臉紅的稱號。
畢業最捨不得的，不是這間學校，是那個只有在這群人面前，才會出現的、有綽號的自己。

en.content:
Once you're out in the working world,
no one will ever call you by that nickname again.

The one only your college friends understood,
named after some dumb thing you did—
it'll surface exactly once at a reunion,
right before everyone laughs till they cry.

So while you still can, say it a few more times.
en.editorNote: For the crew that gave each other nicknames nobody outside the group would ever get; tag them and watch the replies flood in
variations: Your future coworkers will only call you by your full name. Only these people remember the ridiculous nickname you earned from one dumb thing you did.
The hardest part of leaving isn't the school. It's leaving behind the version of you—the one with the nickname—that only existed around these people.

items.sourceNote: 2026 社群流行語「班味」，新鮮人入職一個月，原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
畢業一個月，
我照鏡子的時候嚇了一跳。

那個上課會偷睡、下課會亂叫的人不見了，
站在那裡的是一個
反射性回答「好的收到」的生物。

原來班味這種東西，
是不用學就會的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛上班一個月的新鮮人發限動；「班味」是近年最有共鳴的職場自嘲詞，配一張通勤自拍或加班桌面照都很搭
variations: 以前被說臉很臭，是因為熬夜打遊戲；現在被說臉很臭，是因為我真的在上班。
畢業典禮那天我還笑得出來，現在連自拍都要重拍五次才有表情，這就是傳說中的職場變身術。

en.content:
One month after graduation,
I caught my own reflection and froze.

The person who napped through lectures
and yelled down the hallway is gone.
Standing there is some creature
that says 'sounds good, will do' on reflex.

Turns out that office-worker aura
is something nobody has to teach you.
en.editorNote: For the new grad one month into their first job; pair it with a commute selfie or a photo of your desk at 8 p.m.
variations: I used to look wrecked because I was up all night gaming. Now I look wrecked because I'm actually employed.
I could still smile on graduation day. Now it takes five takes to get one selfie where I look alive. They transform you fast.

items.sourceNote: 退宿搬家場景，原創溫情向

zh-tw.content:
退宿那天才發現，
住了四年的房間，
三個紙箱就搬空了。

搬不走的是牆上
貼海報留下的那塊痕跡，
還有半夜三點
有人陪你笑到肚子痛的那種聲音。

箱子很輕，我卻有點抬不動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合搬離宿舍或租屋處那天發文，配一張搬空的房間照最有後勁；也很適合直接傳給一起住過的那個人
variations: 四年的青春，最後被壓縮成三個紙箱和一張退宿單。押金退回來的那一刻，我才真的畢業了。
房間空了以後才明白，讓那裡變成家的，從來不是那些傢俱。

en.content:
On move-out day I found out
that the room I lived in for four years
fits into three cardboard boxes.

What doesn't fit is the mark on the wall
where a poster used to hang,
and the sound of someone laughing with you
until your stomach hurt at 3 a.m.

The boxes are light. I can barely lift them.
en.editorNote: Post it the day you move out, with a photo of the emptied room; quiet in the moment, hits you hours later. Also a good message to send the person you shared it with
variations: Four years of my life, compressed into three boxes and one move-out form. The moment the deposit hit my account, I actually graduated.
Only after the room was empty did I understand: it was never the furniture that made it home.

items.sourceNote: 2026 新鮮人求職心態，試用期雙向選擇，原創

zh-tw.content:
公司給我三個月試用期。

沒問題，
我也在試用這間公司。

畢業以後最該學會的一課是：
被挑選的同時，
你也有資格挑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛入職、或正在猶豫要不要留下的新鮮人；把「試用期」翻轉成雙向選擇，比一味勸人忍耐更有力量
variations: 面試那天他們在評估我值不值得，我也在心裡算，這裡值不值得我留三年。這場考試從來就不是單向的。
第一份工作不是終點，是實驗。不合適就換，這不叫抗壓性差，這叫你還記得自己要什麼。

en.content:
They gave me a three-month probation period.

No problem.
I'm evaluating them too.

The most useful lesson after graduation:
being chosen and choosing
are supposed to happen at the same time.
en.editorNote: For a new hire finding their footing, or anyone quietly weighing whether to stay; framing probation as mutual beats telling people to just tough it out
variations: In that interview they were deciding if I was worth it. I was running the same math on them. The test was never one-directional.
Your first job isn't a destination, it's an experiment. Walking away from a bad fit isn't weakness — it means you still remember what you wanted.

items.sourceNote: 學生證失效、學生優惠掰掰，原創生活哏

zh-tw.content:
畢業最痛的一刻，
不是撥穗，也不是說再見。

是我在電影院掏出學生證，
店員很有禮貌地說：
「同學，這張過期囉。」

就那一秒，我真的長大了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後第一次被拒絕學生優惠時發，是很生活、很小的失落，留言區保證一堆人喊「我也是」
variations: 以前覺得半價是理所當然，現在才知道，那是學校最後偷偷塞給我的獎學金。
我的臉沒變，學生證過期了，價目表卻很誠實地提醒我：你現在是大人，請付全額。

en.content:
The most painful moment of graduating
isn't the ceremony, and it isn't the goodbyes.

It's pulling out my student ID at the theater
and hearing the clerk say, very politely,
that it expired last month.

That one second right there. That's when I grew up.
en.editorNote: Post it the first time you get turned down for a student discount; a tiny, painfully relatable loss that fills the comments with 'same'
variations: I always thought the student price was just what things cost. Turns out it was the last scholarship the school ever slipped me.
My face hasn't changed. My student ID expired. And the price list is very honest about which of those matters.

items.sourceNote: 「精神離職」流行語的校園版改寫，原創

zh-tw.content:
其實我大四下就精神畢業了，
學校只是比較晚才發現。

人在教室，心在租屋處；
報告有交，靈魂沒有。

今天終於補辦完手續，
人跟心正式合體。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合最後一學期躺平躺到底的人發畢業文，自嘲又不失可愛；是「精神離職」的校園版，很適合轉傳到系上群組
variations: 最後一學期我唯一認真投入的事，是精算還能翹幾堂課不會被當。這也是一種專業。
畢業典禮那天我沒什麼感覺，因為我的心半年前就先走了，今天只是禮貌上回來簽個名。

en.content:
Honestly, I graduated in spirit
sometime during my last semester.
The school just took a while to notice.

Body in the classroom, mind back at my apartment.
Assignments submitted, soul not included.

Today I finally filed the paperwork,
and the two halves of me are reunited.
en.editorNote: For anyone who fully coasted through their final semester; it's the campus version of quiet quitting and it gets forwarded straight to the group chat
variations: The only thing I put real effort into last semester was calculating how many classes I could skip without failing. That's a skill too.
I didn't feel much at the ceremony. My heart left six months ago — it only came back today to be polite and sign its name.

items.sourceNote: 「這張畢業證書上也有你的指紋」友情感謝角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
這張畢業證書上只有我的名字，
但上面有你的指紋。

那些我想放棄的晚上，是你把我拖回書桌前。
那些我以為過不了的關，是你陪我熬到天亮。

所以嚴格來說，
這是我們一起畢業的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業時傳給那個一路陪你撐過來的死黨，把功勞分一半給對方，比單純說謝謝更有份量，配畢業合照發特別戳心
variations: 如果畢業證書可以寫兩個名字，我一定把你的名字放在我旁邊。

en.content:
This diploma only has my name on it,
but your fingerprints are all over it.

Every night I wanted to quit, you dragged me back to my desk.
Every wall I thought I couldn't climb, you stayed up until sunrise with me.

So technically,
we graduated together.
en.editorNote: For the friend who carried you through — splitting the credit lands harder than a plain thank-you, especially paired with a photo of the two of you
variations: If a diploma could hold two names, yours would be right next to mine.

items.sourceNote: 「出社會沒附說明書」學校教的與現實脫節，搞笑角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
讀了十六年書，
學校教了微積分、三角函數、還有光合作用，
就是沒教怎麼報稅、怎麼租房子、怎麼跟房東殺價。

畢業證書到手那天我才發現：
這台叫「大人」的機器，
出廠居然沒附說明書。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛畢業被現實生活搞得一頭霧水的人發文，吐槽學校教的跟出社會要用的完全兩回事，越看越有共鳴
variations: 學校考的都是有標準答案的，出社會考的全是沒有參考解答的申論題。
早知道當年少背一點英文單字，多學一點怎麼看勞健保扣繳。

en.content:
Sixteen years of school taught me calculus, trig, and photosynthesis.
Not once did anyone explain how to file taxes,
sign a lease, or haggle with a landlord.

The day I got my diploma, it finally hit me:
this machine called "adult"
shipped without a manual.
en.editorNote: For the fresh grad drowning in real-life admin — the gap between what school tested and what life tests is painfully relatable
variations: School exams came with answer keys. Real life is all essay questions and no reference solutions.
Wish I'd memorized fewer vocab words and learned how to read a pay stub instead.

items.sourceNote: 畢業=遊戲自動存檔丟進新地圖、無教學關，搞笑角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
畢業就像遊戲自動存檔，
然後把你丟進一張全新的地圖。

沒有教學關，沒有攻略，
連在哪裡復活都不知道。

唯一確定的是——
難度已經幫你調到「現實」模式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合愛打電動的人發畢業文，把出社會比喻成沒有教學關的新地圖，自嘲又貼切；轉到遊戲同好群組保證有人回「難度還不能調回來」
variations: 學生時代是新手村，物價便宜、怪也弱；畢業就是直接被傳送到最終BOSS的門口。
以前被當還能重修，現在人生沒有讀檔這個選項了。

en.content:
Graduation is like the game auto-saving
and dropping you into a brand-new map.

No tutorial, no walkthrough,
you don't even know where you respawn.

Only one thing's certain —
the difficulty's already locked on "reality" mode.
en.editorNote: For the gamers posting their grad pics — framing adulthood as a new map with no tutorial always lands; someone in the group chat will reply "and you can't lower the difficulty"
variations: School was the starter village — cheap prices, weak enemies. Graduation teleports you straight to the final boss's door.
Fail a class and you could retake it. Real life doesn't have a reload button.

items.sourceNote: 畢業=第一幕謝幕而非散場、換舞台，感人出發角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
畢業典禮不是散場，
是這齣戲第一幕的謝幕。

燈會暗一下，
有人會離開這個舞台，
但故事沒有結束——
只是換幕、換場景、換一批還沒登場的角色。

記得，你一直都是主角。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業季送給即將各奔東西的同學，把畢業講成「第一幕謝幕」而不是結束，溫暖又有畫面感，配畢業照發特別對味
variations: 這一幕的燈滅了，不代表你的戲演完了，只代表你要換一個更大的舞台。

en.content:
A graduation isn't the show closing.
It's the curtain call on Act One.

The lights dim for a moment,
some of the cast walk off this stage,
but the story isn't over —
just a new act, a new set, a cast of characters who haven't walked on yet.

Remember: you were always the lead.
en.editorNote: For classmates about to scatter — calling graduation the "curtain call on Act One" instead of an ending is warm and cinematic, perfect with a grad photo
variations: The lights going down on this scene don't mean your part is over — it means you're moving to a bigger stage.

items.sourceNote: 家長視角看孩子畢業，感人，重新創作（既有內容多為學生視角）

zh-tw.content:
好像上禮拜才幫你背上第一個書包，
你回頭跟我揮手，
然後頭也不回地跑進校門。

今天你穿著學士袍站在台上，
又是頭也不回地往前走。

這次我沒有哭。

（好啦，有一點。）
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合爸媽在孩子畢業時發限動或寫進卡片，從家長視角把「第一個書包」和「學士袍」對照，畫面感強又不煽情，比制式的「我以你為榮」更打動人
variations: 你長大的每一步都是往前走，而我學會的，是站在原地為你鼓掌。

en.content:
Feels like just last week I buckled you into your first backpack.
You turned, waved,
then ran through those school gates without looking back.

Today you're up on that stage in a cap and gown,
again walking forward without looking back.

This time I didn't cry.

(Okay. A little.)
en.editorNote: For a parent posting on grad day or writing in a card — pairing "first backpack" with "cap and gown" is vivid and lands harder than a stock "I'm so proud of you"
variations: Every step you take is forward. What I've learned is how to stand still and cheer.

items.sourceNote: 畢業雙關短caption（hotter by one degree類型），搞笑，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
報告各位，
本人今天正式升級一個「度」。

學位＋1，
溫度也＋1。

畢竟越有學問的人，看起來就是越燙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 超短的畢業自誇文，玩「學位」跟「熱度」的雙關，配一張穿學士服的照片發IG最剛好，欠揍但很好笑
variations: 四年只換到一個degree？不，我還順便熱了一度。

en.content:
Announcement:
today I officially went up by one degree.

A degree on paper,
and a degree hotter, obviously.

Education looks good on me.
en.editorNote: A one-line flex caption riding the "hotter by one degree" pun — pair it with a cap-and-gown photo. Cocky, harmless, and gets the likes
variations: Four years for one degree? Nah — I also went up a degree in heat.

items.sourceNote: 極簡反思短caption（chapter closed / onward），感人，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
這一章，讀完了。

下一章還是空白的。

而空白，
是我最喜歡的開始方式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 很短很乾淨的畢業文案，把「下一章空白」講成期待而不是焦慮，適合配畢業照或當限動一句話，留白讓照片說話
variations: 上一頁寫滿了，下一頁還沒動筆——這正是最好的地方。

en.content:
This chapter: finished.

The next one's still blank.

And a blank page
is my favorite way to begin.
en.editorNote: A short, clean caption that reframes the "blank next chapter" as excitement instead of anxiety — perfect as a one-liner over a grad photo, leaving room for the image to speak
variations: Last page: full. Next page: untouched — which is exactly the best part.

items.sourceNote: 「畢業不是終點是綠燈/go signal」勵志角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
別人問我畢業有什麼感覺，
我說：像是等了很久的紅燈，
終於變綠燈了。

終點線？不，那是起跑燈。
可以走了，
而且這次沒有人幫你決定方向。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業季當限動或IG caption，把「畢業」重新定義成綠燈而不是終點，語氣正向又不老套，特別適合對未來還有點緊張的人
variations: 畢業不是抵達，是綠燈亮了——路是你的，油門也是你的。

en.content:
Someone asked how graduation feels.
I said: like a red light you waited forever at
finally turning green.

A finish line? No.
It's the go signal —
and this time nobody picks the direction for you.
en.editorNote: A positive, non-cliché caption that reframes graduation as a green light instead of a finish line — great for the class of 2026 who feel a little nervous about what comes next
variations: Graduation isn't arrival. It's the light turning green — the road is yours, and so is the gas pedal.

items.sourceNote: 「officially out of office」離職自動回覆口吻寫畢業，搞笑角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
最終公告：
本人正式離開學校辦公室，
無限期不再上課、不再交作業、不再被點名。

自動回覆已開啟。

（三個月後將於某公司辦公室重新上線，
職稱：菜鳥。）
zh-tw.editorNote: 用「離職自動回覆」的口吻寫畢業，反差感很強，適合傳給同樣要進職場的同學，或當自嘲式IG貼文
variations: 畢業 = 從一間辦公室無縫轉調到另一間辦公室，差別是這次要打卡、領薪水。

en.content:
Final announcement:
I am now officially out of office.
No more classes, no more assignments, no more roll call.

Auto-reply is on.

(Back online in three months at a different office.
New title: rookie.)
en.editorNote: Written like a resignation auto-reply — the contrast lands well; send it to classmates heading into the workforce or post it as a self-deprecating caption
variations: Graduation = a seamless transfer from one office to another. The difference: this one clocks you in and pays you.

items.sourceNote: 把文憑當昂貴商品吐槽（無保固/不能退貨），搞笑＋現實角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
這張畢業證書是我買過最貴的東西，
卻沒有保固、不能退貨、
也沒有客服可以打。

用了才發現：
它保證你「讀完了」，
但不保證你「用得到」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把文憑當成一件昂貴商品來吐槽，戳中很多人「學費 vs 實用度」的無奈，適合半自嘲的畢業貼文
variations: 文憑這件商品：不能退貨、沒有保固，唯一保證的功能是證明你付得起。

en.content:
This diploma is the most expensive thing I've ever bought,
and it comes with no warranty,
no refunds,
and no customer support line.

Turns out it guarantees you finished —
not that you'll ever use it.
en.editorNote: Roasts the degree like an overpriced product — nails the tuition-versus-usefulness feeling; perfect for a half-joking grad post
variations: The diploma: non-refundable, no warranty, no returns. But hey — payment successful.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後友情慢慢淡掉（「明天見」變成沒再說出口），感人角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
我們從來沒有好好說再見。

只是有一天，
「明天見」變成了「有空約」，
然後「有空約」也慢慢沒人再提。

不是不在乎，
是我們都被推著往前走了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫出畢業後友情最真實的樣子——沒有正式的告別，只是「明天見」慢慢消失，適合傳給那個以前每天見、現在很久沒聯絡的同學
variations: 畢業沒有告別式，只有一句再也沒說出口的「明天見」。

en.content:
We never really said goodbye.

One day, "see you tomorrow"
quietly turned into "let's catch up sometime,"
and then nobody brought up "sometime" anymore.

It wasn't that we stopped caring.
Life just kept nudging us forward.
en.editorNote: Captures how post-graduation friendships actually fade — no formal goodbye, just a "see you tomorrow" that slowly disappears; send it to the friend you used to see every day
variations: Graduation has no farewell ceremony — only a "see you tomorrow" that never got said again.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後學校信箱與雲端硬碟停用、四年檔案要搬家的真實情境，感人＋現實角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
學校寄來一封信，
說我的帳號再過三十天就會停用，
請盡快把資料備份。

我打開那顆雲端硬碟，
裡面是四年的報告、
沒交出去的作品集、
還有一堆連檔名都懶得取的照片。

原來畢業不只是離開，
還要親手把自己搬到別的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 畢業一兩個月後才會遇到的真實時刻——學校信箱與雲端空間到期，被迫整理四年的檔案；適合搬檔案搬到一半突然情緒上來時發的貼文
variations: 備份進度 87%，回憶進度 0%。
刪掉重複檔案很快，刪掉那幾張合照卻按不下去。

en.content:
The school emailed to say
my account gets shut off in thirty days,
so please back everything up.

I opened the drive and found
four years of papers,
a portfolio I never sent anywhere,
and hundreds of photos I never bothered to name.

Turns out graduating isn't just leaving.
It's packing yourself up and moving out.
en.editorNote: The real moment that hits a month or two after the ceremony — your student email and cloud storage expire and you're forced to sort through four years; good for a post written mid-download
variations: Backup: 87% complete. Me: 0% complete.
Deleting duplicate files is easy. Deleting that one group photo isn't.

items.sourceNote: 台灣男生畢業後在等錄取通知與兵單之間的黑色幽默，搞笑＋現實角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
同學都在等錄取通知，
我在等兵單。

差別是：
他們可能等不到，
我一定等得到。

這大概是我人生中
第一份不用面試、
百分之百會上的工作。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫給畢業後卡在求職與入伍之間的男生，用「一定會錄取」的反差自嘲；適合收到兵單那天發限動
variations: 履歷投了二十封沒回音，唯一主動聯絡我的是國家。
職涯規劃：先服役，再服軟。

en.content:
My classmates are waiting on job offers.
I'm waiting on my draft notice.

The difference is:
theirs might never come.
Mine definitely will.

Probably the only position I'll ever land
with zero interviews
and a hundred percent acceptance rate.
en.editorNote: For guys stuck between job hunting and mandatory service after graduation — leans on the joke that one 'employer' always says yes; good for the day the notice arrives
variations: Twenty applications, zero replies. The only one who wrote back was the government.
Career plan: serve first, sell out later.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後第一個沒有開學日的夏天、暑假不會結束的失重感，感人＋迷茫角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
以前的暑假之所以快樂，
是因為它會結束。

今年這個沒有結束日。

沒有開學、沒有課表、
沒有人在群組裡問「幾點的課」。

自由這麼大一片攤在眼前，
我卻第一次覺得，
有點站不穩。
zh-tw.editorNote: 七、八月最有共鳴的畢業後心情——不是捨不得典禮，而是發現這個暑假不會被開學接住；適合半夜睡不著時發的長文開頭
variations: 第一次遇到一個不會被開學結束的暑假。
以前放假是暫停鍵，現在放假是空白鍵。

en.content:
Summer used to be great
because it ended.

This one doesn't.

No first day back, no class schedule,
nobody texting the group chat
asking what time lecture starts.

All that freedom spread out in front of me,
and for the first time
I can't quite find my footing.
en.editorNote: The July-August version of post-grad feelings — not missing the ceremony, but realizing no semester is coming to catch you; works as the opening of a late-night caption
variations: My first summer that no school year will ever end.
Break used to be the pause button. Now it's just blank space.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後自我介紹失去現成標籤、被問「你現在在做什麼」的尷尬，搞笑＋迷茫角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
以前自我介紹很簡單：
哪間學校、哪個系、大幾。

三句話，身分就到位了。

現在有人問我在做什麼，
我卡了三秒，
只好說：「還在看機會。」

原來最難寫的自傳那一欄，
是「現在」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 戳中畢業後最尷尬的社交時刻——沒有現成標籤可以介紹自己；適合待業期或轉換期的自嘲貼文
variations: 學校至少會發一個身分給你，社會不會。
「還在看機會」是新鮮人最萬用的四個字。

en.content:
Introducing myself used to be easy:
school, major, year.

Three facts and everyone knew who I was.

Now someone asks what I'm doing
and I stall for three seconds
before landing on "still exploring options."

Turns out the hardest line to write
isn't where I've been.
It's where I am.
en.editorNote: Nails the most awkward post-grad small talk — no ready-made label to hand people; good for a self-deprecating post during the in-between months
variations: School hands you an identity. The real world makes you build one.
"Still exploring options" is doing a lot of heavy lifting this summer.

items.sourceNote: 畢業兩個月後同學各自進入不同節奏（上班、入伍、待業、出國）造成的距離感，感人＋友情角度，重新創作

zh-tw.content:
才過兩個月，
我們就活成了四種時間。

有人已經在打卡上班，
有人剃了頭進了部隊，
有人還在投履歷，
有人整理行李準備出國。

訊息還是會回，
只是回得越來越慢——
不是感情變淡，
是我們的一天，
已經對不上了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 寫畢業後最真實的疏遠：不是吵架也不是誰的錯，只是作息與人生階段錯開了；適合傳給那個很久沒約成的同學
variations: 我們沒有走散，只是時區不一樣了。
群組還在，只是大家都在不同的小時裡活著。

en.content:
Two months out
and we're already living in four different clocks.

One of us clocks in at nine,
one shaved his head and shipped out,
one is still sending applications,
one is packing for a flight.

We still reply.
Just slower every time —
not because we care less,
but because our days
stopped lining up.
en.editorNote: The honest version of drifting apart after graduation — no fight, no villain, just schedules and life stages that no longer match; send it to the friend you keep failing to meet up with
variations: We didn't lose each other. We just live in different time zones now.
The group chat is still there. We're all just awake in different hours.

items.sourceNote: 畢業留言冊懷舊報導：當年寫下的留言，多年後重讀才讀出不同意思，感人＋回憶角度重新創作

zh-tw.content:
紀念冊被我塞在書櫃最上層，
畢業那天以後就沒再翻開。

上禮拜找東西才翻到，
看到你寫給我的那一頁。

當時只覺得你在亂寫，
這次讀完，
我坐在地板上看了三分鐘。

有些話是這樣的——
寫的時候是玩笑，
要等到你真的需要它那天，
才會變成真的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業幾個月後整理房間翻到紀念冊的貼文；也可以直接寫進別人的紀念冊，當成留言的結尾
variations: 當年隨手寫的那句，後來替我撐過一個晚上。
紀念冊最好的地方，是它會等到你讀懂為止。

en.content:
The yearbook went to the top shelf
and stayed shut after that day.

I found it last week looking for something else,
and landed on the page you wrote me.

Back then I figured you were just goofing around.
Reading it this time,
I sat on the floor for three whole minutes.

Some lines work like that —
written as a joke,
and they don't come true
until the day you actually need them.
en.editorNote: For the post-grad months, when you find the yearbook while cleaning your room; also works as the closing line when you're the one signing someone else's
variations: The throwaway line you wrote me ended up carrying me through a bad night.
The best thing about a yearbook is that it waits until you're ready to read it.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後「鬧鐘不用設了」的網路貼文，改寫成捨不得刪掉早八鬧鐘、最後換成上班鬧鐘的角度

zh-tw.content:
畢業快兩個月了，
手機裡那個叫「早八」的鬧鐘，
我一直沒刪。

它已經不用叫我起床，
但每天七點十分還是震一下，
像在問我：
「今天要去哪？」

昨天我終於把它關掉了。
然後設了一個新的。

這次沒有課名，
只寫了兩個字——上班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 用手機鬧鐘標籤的變化寫身分交接，比喊口號更有感；適合開始上班前一週的貼文，或收到offer那天的限動
variations: 刪掉早八那個鬧鐘，比走出校門那天更像畢業。
鬧鐘還是七點響，只是它現在叫我去的地方會發薪水。

en.content:
Almost two months out
and I still haven't deleted
the alarm labeled "8AM LECTURE."

It doesn't wake me for anything now,
but 7:10 rolls around
and it buzzes once anyway,
like it's asking:
"So where are we going today?"

Yesterday I finally switched it off
and set a new one.

No course name this time.
Just: work.
en.editorNote: Marks the handover of identity through a phone alarm label instead of a big speech; good for the week before your first job, or a story post the day you sign the offer
variations: Deleting that 8AM alarm felt more like graduating than the ceremony did.
Same 7am buzz. The place it sends me to just pays now.

items.sourceNote: 網路討論：畢業後系服多半淪為睡衣或做家事穿，改寫成把系服擬人化、幫它寫職涯發展的搞笑版

zh-tw.content:
畢業之後，
那件系服的職涯發展如下：

第一個月：捨不得穿，掛著。
第二個月：睡衣。
第三個月：擦地板。

它比我先找到工作，
而且已經升遷兩次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 畢業後每個人衣櫃都有的那件系服，用職涯口吻寫最好笑；適合待業期自嘲貼文或系上群組哏圖配字
variations: 我還在等回信，我的系服已經進入管理職。
系服的職涯規劃比我清楚，它一路往下但很穩定。

en.content:
Career path of my college class shirt
since graduation:

Month one: too precious to wear. On a hanger.
Month two: pajamas.
Month three: floor rag.

It found work before I did,
and it's already been promoted twice.
en.editorNote: Everyone has that one class shirt in the closet; the corporate-career framing is what makes it land — good for a self-deprecating job-hunt post
variations: I'm still waiting on callbacks. My class shirt is already middle management.
My class shirt has a clearer career plan than I do. Downward, but stable.

items.sourceNote: post-graduation transition themes: moving out, first job, life after campus

zh-tw.content:
退租那天，我把房間搬空了。

床墊立起來、貼紙一張一張撕掉、
牆上的釘孔用牙膏補起來。

弄完站在門口看，
它跟四年前我第一次走進來時
長得一模一樣。

原來這個房間從來沒有變成我的。
我只是在裡面住了四年，
然後把它還回去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 搬離租屋處那天發限動最有感，配一張空房間的照片；也適合寫在搬家日記或給室友的訊息裡
variations: 把租屋處還原成四年前的樣子，才發現我留下的東西一件都帶不走。
房間清空的那一刻我才懂：不是我離開它，是我一直只是暫住。

en.content:
Moved out today.

Mattress tipped on its side,
stickers peeled off one by one,
nail holes in the wall patched with toothpaste.

When I finished I stood in the doorway,
and it looked exactly the way it did
the first time I walked in four years ago.

The room never became mine.
I just lived in it for a while,
then handed it back.
en.editorNote: Post it the day you hand back the keys, paired with a photo of the empty room; also works as a caption for a moving-out carousel
variations: Restored the apartment to how it looked four years ago and realized none of what I left behind fits in a box.
The second the room was empty I got it: I wasn't leaving it. I was only ever borrowing it.

items.sourceNote: first-job expectations vs reality for new graduates

zh-tw.content:
手機震了一下，銀行的入帳通知。

數字比我想像的小，
扣完該扣的之後更小。

但我還是盯著那串數字看了很久。

以前戶頭裡的每一筆，
都是別人給我的。

這是第一筆，
是我自己換來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 領到第一份薪水那天發最準，配一張薪轉通知或午餐照；也適合寫給同樣剛開始工作的朋友
variations: 第一份薪水沒有想像中多，但它是第一筆不用跟任何人說謝謝的錢。
看著入帳通知才發現，長大不是變有錢，是錢終於變成自己的。

en.content:
My phone buzzed. Deposit notification.

The number was smaller than I pictured,
and smaller still after the deductions.

I stared at it for a long time anyway.

Every amount that ever landed in that account
was given to me.

This is the first one
I traded something for.
en.editorNote: Perfect for the day your first paycheck clears — pair it with a screenshot or your first bought-it-myself meal
variations: First paycheck was less than I hoped and still the first money I didn't have to thank anyone for.
Growing up isn't having more money. It's the money finally being yours.

items.sourceNote: advice pieces for new entrants to the workforce

zh-tw.content:
拿到人生第一盒名片。

以前我的名字前面印的是校名，
現在換成了公司名。

有點不習慣。
但仔細看——

中間那一行從頭到尾沒有換過。

上面那行以後還會再換很多次，
真正要自己撐住的，
是中間那一行。
zh-tw.editorNote: 報到第一週拿到名片時發，配名片照；也適合送給剛換跑道的朋友當鼓勵
variations: 名片上的頭銜會一直換，名字只有一個，先把名字做好。
校名、公司名都是暫時借你的，只有中間那三個字要跟你一輩子。

en.content:
Got my first box of business cards.

My name used to sit under a school's name.
Now it sits under a company's.

Still getting used to that.
But look closer —

the line in the middle never changed.

The line above it will change many more times.
The one you actually have to hold up
is the one in the middle.
en.editorNote: Great for your first week at a new job, paired with a photo of the card; also works as encouragement for a friend switching careers
variations: Titles keep changing. You only get one name — build that one first.
School names and company names are both on loan. The name in the middle is the only one that stays.

items.sourceNote: community posts about revisiting campus after graduating

zh-tw.content:
「同學，你找誰？」

上禮拜回學校拿東西，
門口的警衛這樣問我。

我愣了兩秒才答得出來。

以前這題的答案是「我住這」，
現在只剩下一個系辦公室的名字。

那條路我閉著眼睛都會走，
但那天從校門走到系館，
我沒遇到半個認識的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 畢業後第一次回學校時發，配校門或空教室的照片；也適合當回憶向的長文開頭
variations: 回學校那天才發現，路一點都沒變，變的是路上沒有人再叫我的名字。
被警衛問「你找誰」的那一秒，我才真的畢業。

en.content:
"Who are you here to see?"

That's what the guard at the gate asked me
when I went back to campus last week
to pick something up.

It took me two seconds to answer.

That question used to have an easy answer: I live here.
Now all I had was the name of a department office.

I could walk that path with my eyes shut,
but that day, gate to building,
I passed nobody I knew.
en.editorNote: For your first trip back to campus after graduating — pair with a shot of the gate or an empty classroom
variations: Went back and nothing about the route had changed. What changed is that nobody on it says my name anymore.
Getting asked who I was there to see is the moment I actually graduated.

items.sourceNote: discussion of the gap between graduating and starting work, resume gaps

zh-tw.content:
四年。

一千四百多天、
三十幾門課、
兩科差點被當、
還有數不清在系館吃泡麵配報告的晚上。

投履歷的時候，
這些全部濃縮成短短一行。

沒關係。
那些塞不進去的，
本來就不是要給人資看的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合投履歷投到懷疑人生時發，配一張履歷截圖或畢業照；也可以當作寫給自己的安慰
variations: 履歷上那一行寫得下學歷，寫不下那四年到底發生過什麼。
四年壓成一行字，剩下的都存在我自己這邊。

en.content:
Four years.

Fourteen hundred-something days,
thirty-odd courses,
two classes I nearly failed,
and more instant-noodle-and-deadline nights
than I can count.

On a resume, all of it compresses
into a single line.

That's fine.
Everything that didn't fit
was never for the recruiter anyway.
en.editorNote: For the stretch of job hunting where the applications blur together — pair with a resume screenshot or a grad photo
variations: One line fits the degree. It doesn't fit what those four years actually were.
Four years compressed to one line. I kept the rest.

items.sourceNote: new-graduate threads about moving out and living alone for the first time

zh-tw.content:
畢業之後我學會的第一件事，
不是什麼專業技能。

是電鍋外鍋要放幾杯水。

第二件事是垃圾車幾點來，
第三件是原來衛生紙
不會自己出現在架子上。

學校教我怎麼分析、怎麼報告，
沒教我一個人住有多安靜。

可是這些我也都學會了。
慢慢地、有點狼狽地，
但是學會了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合搬出來自己住的第一個月發，配一張自己煮的失敗料理或空房間照片
variations: 四年寫得出論文，卻花了三天才搞懂垃圾車的路線。
會分析五力模型，不會分辨洗衣精跟柔軟精。這也算成長吧。

en.content:
The first thing I learned after graduating
wasn't a professional skill.

It was how much water goes in the rice cooker.

Second was what day the trash gets picked up.
Third was that toilet paper
doesn't restock itself.

School taught me how to analyze things,
how to present them.
It never mentioned
how quiet an apartment gets
when it's only yours.

But I'm learning that too.
Slowly. Clumsily.
Still learning it.
en.editorNote: For the first month of living alone — pair with a failed home-cooked meal or an empty room
variations: I can write a thesis. It took me three days to figure out the trash schedule.
Four years of critical thinking, and I still stared at the detergent aisle for ten minutes.

items.sourceNote: workplace survival advice for first-job graduates, on asking questions

zh-tw.content:
上班第一週我最怕的
不是做錯事，
是問問題。

怕被覺得笨、
怕前輩嫌煩、
怕自己不夠格坐在這裡。

後來我發現，
學校那四年一直有人主動教我，
出社會之後沒有了——

沒有人會追著你講解，
你不問，就真的沒人講。

所以現在我問。
問得很爛，但我問。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職第一個月分享，也適合鼓勵同期入職的朋友
variations: 在學校不懂會有人講，出社會不懂只會有人等你自己發現。
問問題會尷尬三分鐘，不問會尷尬一整個專案。

en.content:
My first week on the job,
what scared me most
wasn't messing up.

It was asking questions.

Scared of looking slow.
Scared of bothering people.
Scared someone would notice
I didn't belong at that desk yet.

Then it hit me:
for four years, someone always explained things
whether I asked or not.
Nobody does that here.

If you don't ask, nobody tells you.

So now I ask.
Badly. But I ask.
en.editorNote: For the first month at a first job, or to encourage a friend starting the same week
variations: In school, not knowing gets explained. At work, not knowing just sits there.
Asking is awkward for three minutes. Not asking is awkward for the whole project.

items.sourceNote: graduates who delay job hunting for exams or further study

zh-tw.content:
八月了。

同學的動態一個接一個變成
「到職第一天」、
「新環境請多指教」，
而我還在同一間自習室、
寫同一本考古題。

有時候會覺得自己被留在原地。

可是比賽不是只有一種賽制。
有人打完九局就下場，
有人的畢業是延長賽——

打比較久，
不代表打得比較差。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合準備研究所、國考、證照的畢業生，看到同學陸續就業時發
variations: 他們的畢業是終點線，我的畢業是延長賽。都還在場上就好。
同一間自習室坐到第三個月。我的比賽只是還沒吹哨。

en.content:
It's August.

One by one, my classmates' feeds turn into
"first day at the new job,"
"excited for this next chapter,"
and I'm still in the same study room,
working through the same practice exams.

Some days it feels like
everyone left and forgot me here.

But not every game runs the same length.
Some people walk off after nine innings.
Some of us graduated into extra innings —

playing longer
isn't the same as playing worse.
en.editorNote: For grads studying for entrance exams or licenses while friends start jobs
variations: Their graduation was a finish line. Mine turned into extra innings. Still on the field.
Third month in the same study room. My game just hasn't called it yet.

items.sourceNote: essays on the quiet months after graduation, once the ceremony fades

zh-tw.content:
畢業典禮那幾天，
每個人的動態都是學士服。

現在八月了。
沒有人再發畢業照，
學士服早就還回去、押金也退了。

那一頁是這時候才真的翻過去的——
不是在典禮上，
是在某個沒有人提起它的平常下午。

有點空。
但空出來的地方，
是要放新東西的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業季熱度退去後的八月發，配空白牆面、新租處或通勤路上的照片
variations: 學士服還回去那天沒哭，是後來才發現不會再穿了。
畢業不是典禮那天結束的，是在沒有人再提起它的那天。

en.content:
During graduation week,
everyone's feed was caps and gowns.

It's August now.
Nobody posts those photos anymore.
The gown went back weeks ago;
the deposit already cleared.

That's when the page actually turned —
not at the ceremony,
but on some ordinary afternoon
when nobody mentioned it at all.

It feels a little empty.
But empty is just
room for what comes next.
en.editorNote: For August, after graduation season fades — pair with a blank wall, a new apartment, or a commute shot
variations: I didn't cry returning the gown. It hit later, realizing I'd never put one on again.
Graduation didn't end at the ceremony. It ended the day nobody brought it up.

items.sourceNote: checklists and first-day-at-work advice aimed at new graduates

zh-tw.content:
到職前一晚，
我打開衣櫃找明天要穿的。

然後發現一個問題：
裡面沒有一件衣服，
是給「上班的我」穿的。

系服、球衣、
三件同款不同色的素T、
還有一件面試那天穿的襯衫。

最後我把那件襯衫
又燙了一次。

四年的衣櫃，
只有一件撐得住明天。
沒關係，
剩下的可以慢慢買。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職前一晚發，配燙好的襯衫、擺在椅背上的衣服或空衣架；也適合寫給同期入職的朋友
variations: 衣櫃裡有四年的大學生活，卻只有一件明天穿得出門。
人生第一件襯衫燙了兩次，不是怕皺，是不知道還能做什麼。

en.content:
The night before my first day,
I opened the closet
to pick out what I'd wear.

And hit a problem:
nothing in there
belonged to the version of me
who starts work tomorrow.

Club shirts. A jersey.
Three identical tees in different colors.
And the one button-down
I wore to the interview.

So I ironed that shirt
a second time.

Four years in a closet,
and exactly one thing
can carry tomorrow.

That's fine.
The rest I can buy slowly.
en.editorNote: For the night before starting a first job — pair with a pressed shirt, clothes laid over a chair, or an empty hanger
variations: My closet holds four years of college and exactly one outfit that works tomorrow.
Ironed the shirt twice. Not because of wrinkles — I just didn't know what else to do with my hands.

items.sourceNote: threads about staying in touch with juniors and classmates after leaving school

zh-tw.content:
昨天有個學妹傳訊息問我，
那門課要不要選、
那個教授會不會很硬。

我一邊回一邊愣住——
這些答案我居然全部都有。

大一的時候，
是我在問這些問題的。
那時候覺得學長姐好像什麼都懂。

原來他們也沒有，
只是先走了兩年而已。

現在換我了。
我也沒有比較懂，
但我可以先告訴你路長什麼樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後第一次被學弟妹請教時發，也適合送給即將入學的新生或剛接棒的幹部
variations: 學長姐不是比較厲害，只是比你早跌一次而已。
從問問題的人變成被問的人，中間好像也沒發生什麼，就四年。

en.content:
A first-year messaged me yesterday
asking whether to take a certain course,
whether that professor grades hard.

I was halfway through my reply
when it stopped me:
I actually had all the answers.

Freshman year, I was the one asking.
Back then the upperclassmen
seemed to know everything.

Turns out they didn't.
They'd just gone two years ahead.

Now it's my turn.
I don't know any more than you do.
But I can tell you
what the road looks like.
en.editorNote: For the first time a junior asks you for advice after you've graduated — also works as a note to incoming students
variations: Upperclassmen aren't smarter. They just tripped on it first.
I went from asking the questions to answering them, and all that happened in between was four years.

items.sourceNote: posts about whether classmates really keep in touch after graduating

zh-tw.content:
凌晨一點，
我點開你的對話框。

上一則是六月，
你問我畢業照要幾點集合。

我打了「在忙嗎」——刪掉。
打了「最近好嗎」——太客套，刪掉。
打了「欸」——又覺得太突然。

最後我傳了一張很爛的迷因。

三分鐘後你回：
「哈哈哈幹你還活著喔」

那一刻我就知道，
沒有生疏，
只是都太久沒有人先開口。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合想聯絡很久沒說話的同學時發，或直接當成傳出去的那一句；也適合放在久違聚會的合照下
variations: 我們沒有變生疏，只是都在等對方先傳第一句。
傳「在忙嗎」很難，傳一張爛梗圖很簡單。友情有時候就靠這個活下來。

en.content:
One in the morning,
I open our chat.

Last message: June.
You were asking what time
we had to line up for grad photos.

I type "you busy?" — delete.
"How've you been?" — too formal, delete.
"Hey" — too abrupt.

In the end I just send
a genuinely terrible meme.

Three minutes later:
"LMAO you're alive??"

And that's when I knew.
Nothing had gone cold.
We were both just waiting
for the other one to go first.
en.editorNote: For when you want to message a classmate you haven't spoken to in months — or just send it as the message itself
variations: We didn't drift. We were both waiting on the other to send the first text.
"You busy?" is hard to send. A bad meme is easy. Friendships survive on this.

items.sourceNote: new-graduate chatter about coworkers and classmates starting jobs at different times

zh-tw.content:
六月的時候，
聯絡人清單裡每個人的大頭貼
都是學士服。

八月開始陸續換掉了。

有人換成識別證，
有人換成理平頭的自拍，
有人換成機場，
有人換成貓。

只有我還是那張畢業照。

不是懶，
是我還想不到
下一張要放什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業兩個月後還沒定下來時發，帶點自嘲但不苦；也適合當作 IG 換頭貼的說明
variations: 別人的大頭貼都升級了，我的還停在六月。
換頭貼這種事，等我知道自己現在是誰再說。

en.content:
Back in June,
every contact in my phone
had the same profile picture:
cap and gown.

August, they started changing.

One swapped in a work badge.
One, a buzzcut selfie.
One, an airport.
One, a cat.

Mine is still the grad photo.

Not laziness.
I just haven't figured out
what the next picture
is supposed to be.
en.editorNote: For the two-months-out stretch when nothing has landed yet — self-deprecating without being bleak
variations: Everyone's profile picture got promoted. Mine is still stuck in June.
I'll change the photo once I know who's supposed to be in it.

items.sourceNote: 2026 reporting on new grads facing automated resume screening, long personality tests and video intros

zh-tw.content:
投出去的第一百封履歷，
系統十二秒後回我：
「感謝您的應徵，我們將保留您的資料。」

在那之前我做了什麼？
一份一百七十二題的性格測驗、
一段對著鏡頭講九十秒的自我介紹、
還有一張把履歷再打一次的線上表格。

後來我想通一件事：
我不是被拒絕，
是還沒輪到人類看到我。

那是兩回事。
所以第一百零一封，我照樣投。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合求職空窗期發，說出被系統篩掉的無力感但收在「不是我的問題」；也適合傳給一起在投履歷的同學
variations: 十二秒就回信的，一定不是人。所以那十二秒，不算數。
一百封履歷換一百封罐頭信。沒關係，罐頭本來就不看人。

en.content:
Application number one hundred.
The system answered in twelve seconds:
"Thank you for your interest. We'll keep your resume on file."

Before that I had filled out
a 172-question personality test,
recorded ninety seconds of my own face,
and retyped my entire resume
into a form that already had my resume.

Then it clicked:
I wasn't rejected.
A human hasn't seen me yet.

Those are not the same thing.
So I sent number one hundred and one.
en.editorNote: For the job-hunt dry spell — names the auto-screening grind without turning bitter
variations: Anything that replies in twelve seconds isn't a person. So those twelve seconds don't count.
A hundred applications, a hundred form letters. Fine. Form letters can't read anyway.

items.sourceNote: new-graduate threads about whether the degree and grades matter once you start working

zh-tw.content:
畢業兩個月，
沒有任何人問過我的成績單。

沒有人問我論文寫什麼、
哪一科差點被當、
書卷拿過幾次。

那張紙從學校拿回來之後，
就一直躺在原本那個塑膠套裡。

一開始我覺得那四年好像白算了。
後來我在會議上被問倒，
回家花兩個晚上把它弄懂——
才發現那四年沒有變成一張紙。

它變成的是：
我還記得怎麼把一件不會的事，
學會。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得學歷派不上用場、懷疑那幾年值不值得的時候發；也適合寫給正在低潮的同學
variations: 沒有人會問你的成績單。但你怎麼把東西弄懂的，會被看見。
四年換到的不是那張紙，是「不會也敢弄懂」這件事。

en.content:
Two months out.
Nobody has asked to see my transcript.

Nobody asked what my thesis was about,
which class I nearly failed,
how many times I made the list.

The diploma is still in the sleeve
it came home in.

At first that felt like four wasted years.
Then someone asked me something in a meeting
I couldn't answer,
and I went home and spent two nights
figuring it out.

That's when I got it.
Those four years didn't turn into paper.
They turned into this:
I still know how to learn a thing
I don't know yet.
en.editorNote: For when the degree feels useless and you're questioning whether school was worth it
variations: No one will ever ask for your transcript. How you figure things out still shows.
The four years didn't buy the paper. They bought the nerve to go learn it.

items.sourceNote: first-week-on-the-job posts from Taiwanese new hires about meeting their onboarding cohort

zh-tw.content:
新人訓第一天，
八個人被塞在同一間會議室，
每個人都在等別人先講話。

中午被放出去吃飯，
在便利商店門口，
有人終於開口：
「欸，剛剛那套系統你聽得懂嗎？」
「完全沒有。」
「太好了，我還以為只有我。」

那一秒我突然發現，
「同學」這種東西沒有結束。

它只是換了一棟樓，
重新分了一次組。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職第一週發，或放在跟同期新人第一頓午餐的合照下
variations: 以為畢業就沒有同學了。結果只是換一間教室、換一群人。
同期就是新的同班同學，差別在這次有薪水。

en.content:
First day of onboarding.
Eight of us in one room,
all waiting for someone else to speak.

At lunch they let us out,
and outside the convenience store
someone finally said:
"Did any of that system training make sense to you?"
"None of it."
"Oh thank god. I thought it was just me."

And right then I got it:
classmates aren't over.

They just moved buildings
and got reassigned.
en.editorNote: For your first week at a new job, or a caption on that first lunch with the other new hires
variations: I thought graduating meant no more classmates. It's just a different room and different people.
Your cohort is your new class. Same panic, except this time it pays.

items.sourceNote: new-hire chatter about pre-employment paperwork and the awkward switch out of student status

zh-tw.content:
到職前要先做體檢。
表格第一頁，
「職業」那一欄，
我拿著筆停了很久。

寫「學生」已經不對了，
寫新職稱又還沒正式上班，
寫「無」感覺太狠。

最後我把職稱寫上去，
自己盯著看了兩秒，
覺得有點好笑，
又有點不習慣。

護理師收走表格的時候只說：
「下一位。」

原來身分轉換這種大事，
在別人眼裡
就只是一張表上的一行字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職前後發，講身分轉換那種微妙的不習慣；也很適合當成報到日的 IG 限動
variations: 人生最難的填空題，是體檢表上「職業」那一格。
四年才拿到那張紙，卻花五分鐘才敢在表格上寫下新的職稱。

en.content:
Pre-employment physical.
Page one, the blank marked
OCCUPATION.

I sat there with the pen up.

"Student" isn't true anymore.
The new title isn't true yet —
I don't start until Monday.
"None" felt a little brutal.

In the end I wrote the title,
stared at it for two seconds,
and felt ridiculous
and unfamiliar at the same time.

The nurse took the form and said:
"Next."

So the biggest identity change of my life
is, to everyone else,
one line on a form.
en.editorNote: For the days around your start date — that odd feeling of a job title that doesn't fit yet
variations: Hardest fill-in-the-blank of my life: OCCUPATION.
Four years for the diploma. Five minutes to write the new title down.

items.sourceNote: new-grad threads about the health-insurance transfer paperwork required when starting a first job

zh-tw.content:
到職那天，人事說要補一張健保轉出單。

我打電話回家問我媽，
她翻了很久的抽屜才找到。

隔天她傳訊息給我：
「好了，你現在自己保了。」
後面還加了一個很醜的貼圖。

我盯著那行字看了一下。

從出生到今天，
我一直掛在她的名下。
現在那一欄變成公司的名字。

沒有典禮，沒有撥穗，
但我覺得那張轉出單，
比畢業證書更像成年禮。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職第一週發，講「正式脫離父母名下」那種安靜的長大；也很適合傳給爸媽看
variations: 真正的畢業證書，是我媽名下那一欄終於少了我的名字。
畢業典禮撥的是穗，成年禮辦的是健保轉出。

en.content:
First day on the job, HR asked me
for a health insurance transfer form.

I called home. Mom went through a drawer
for ten minutes before she found it.

The next day she texted:
"Done. You're on your own plan now."
Plus a sticker.

I read it twice.

Since the day I was born
I'd been listed under her name.
Now that line says a company instead.

No ceremony, no tassel.
But that little form felt more like
growing up
than the diploma ever did.
en.editorNote: For your first week on the job — the quiet, paperwork version of growing up
variations: The real graduation certificate is the day your name comes off your mom's plan.
School handed me a tassel. HR handed me an adult.

items.sourceNote: first-job chatter about accruing paid leave and having none to use in the first six months

zh-tw.content:
同學在群組揪十月出去玩。

我打開系統算了一下：
到職滿六個月才有三天特休，
我還差兩個月。

以前的假是內建的。
行事曆上紅色的那幾格，
不用申請，時間自己會給你。

現在的假要用攢的，
一個月存零點五天，
像在集點換咖啡。

我回群組：
「你們先去，幫我拍照。」

送出之後我坐在位子上想——
原來大人的自由，
是一天一天存出來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合新鮮人上班前幾個月發，講「連放假都要重新學」的落差；配行事曆或請假系統截圖很有感
variations: 學生時代的紅字是放假，出社會的紅字是待辦。
特休存款：零點五天。人生存款：另計。

en.content:
Group chat: everyone's planning a trip in October.

I opened the HR portal and did the math.
Three days of PTO after six months.
I'm two months short.

Time off used to come built in —
the red squares on the calendar,
no request, no approval.

Now I have to save up for it,
half a day a month,
like a coffee punch card.

I typed back:
"Go without me. Send pictures."

Then I sat there and thought:
so this is adult freedom.
You earn it half a day at a time.
en.editorNote: For the first months at a new job, when even taking time off is a skill you have to relearn
variations: In school the red days meant rest. Now they mean deadlines.
PTO balance: 0.5 days. Emotional balance: pending.

items.sourceNote: university library FAQ: licensed e-resources are limited to current students and staff; alumni must use in-library terminals

zh-tw.content:
工作上要查一篇論文。

我照著以前的習慣點下去，
跳出一個從沒看過的視窗：
單篇下載，三十九點九五美金。

以前這個按鈕是免費的。
四年我按過幾百次，
從來沒想過它有價錢。

寫信問學校圖書館，
館員很客氣地回：
校友請親自到館內公用電腦查詢。

原來學生時代最貴的東西不是學費，
是那些我以為本來就免費的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業幾個月後發，講「離開學校才知道什麼叫特權」；也很適合拿來提醒還在學的人把資源用好用滿
variations: 畢業後才發現，那個下載按鈕一直是別人幫我付的。
學生證最貴的功能，是我從來沒注意過的那幾個。

en.content:
Needed a paper for work.

Clicked through out of pure habit
and hit a window I'd never seen:
$39.95 to download. One article.

That button used to be free.
I pressed it a few hundred times in four years
and never once wondered what it cost.

I emailed the library.
The librarian wrote back, very politely:
alumni are welcome to use the terminals here.

Turns out the most expensive thing about being a student
wasn't tuition.
It was everything I assumed was free.
en.editorNote: For a few months out — the things you only recognize as a privilege once they're gone. Also a nudge to current students to use the library while they still can
variations: Nobody mentions that someone else was paying for that download button.
The priciest thing on my student ID was the part I never noticed.

items.sourceNote: posts about clearing out textbooks after graduation and keeping one for the notes in the margins

zh-tw.content:
把系上的專業書整理出來，拿去二手書店。

一整箱，秤完重量，
老闆給了我兩百四。
不夠吃一頓好一點的晚餐。

單子都簽完了，
我又把最上面那本抽回來。

不是因為它比較貴。
是因為第一頁的空白處，
有人用鉛筆幫我畫了一隻很醜的貓，
旁邊寫著「醒醒，還有兩小時」。

其他的我都賣掉了。

那隻貓沒辦法秤重。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合清書櫃、整理房間的時候發；講的是有些東西值錢的不是內容，是旁邊那行字
variations: 整箱書賣了兩百四，其中一本我用零元把大學買回來。
書可以秤斤賣，寫在旁邊那句話不行。

en.content:
Hauled my textbooks to the used bookstore.

A whole box. They weighed it
and handed me twelve dollars.
Not even a decent dinner.

I'd already signed the slip
when I reached back and pulled one out.

Not because it was worth more.
Because on the inside cover
someone had penciled a genuinely terrible cat
with a caption: "wake up, two hours left."

I sold everything else.

That cat doesn't weigh anything.
en.editorNote: For cleaning out the bookshelf — some things are valuable for what's in the margins, not the pages
variations: Sold the whole box for twelve bucks and bought one year of my life back for free.
You can sell books by the pound. Not what someone wrote in the margin.

items.sourceNote: first-job guides and new-hire posts about the shift from a five-minute walk to class to a real rush-hour commute

zh-tw.content:
以前上課前十分鐘才起床，
拖鞋一穿，五分鐘到教室，
遲到最多被點名。

現在我七點出門，
在車廂裡被擠成一片薄片，
一隻手抓吊環，
另一隻手連手機都拿不出來。

到公司八點五十。
還沒開始工作，
今天的力氣已經先用掉三成。

原來上班最累的部分，
是還沒上班的那一段。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合上班第一個月發，講學生通勤跟社畜通勤的落差；配車廂或月台的照片很搭
variations: 大學的距離用分鐘算，上班的距離用體力算。
以前遲到只是被點名，現在遲到要扣錢，而且還得先站一小時。

en.content:
In college I woke up ten minutes before class,
put on slippers,
and was in the room in five.
Worst case, they marked me late.

Now I leave at seven,
get pressed flat in a train car,
one hand on the strap,
the other unable to reach my phone.

I walk in at 8:50.
Haven't started working,
already down thirty percent.

Turns out the hardest part of the job
is the part before the job.
en.editorNote: For your first month commuting — the gap between a five-minute walk to class and an hour on a packed train
variations: College distance was measured in minutes. Work distance is measured in energy.
Being late used to cost me attendance. Now it costs money, plus an hour of standing.

items.sourceNote: university capstone exhibition requirements and design-student posts about the last day of the show and taking the work down

zh-tw.content:
畢業展最後一天，五點閉館。

五點零五分，
我們開始把牆上的東西撕下來。

那面牆花了我們三個晚上才貼好，
水平尺量過，間距對齊過，
有一張歪了兩公釐重貼了四次。

撕下來只花了十一分鐘。

我把作品捲成一捲夾在腋下，
走出展場的時候回頭看了一眼——
剛剛還是我們的那面牆，
現在只是一面白牆。

下禮拜學弟妹要用。

原來所謂的完成，
就是把東西做出來，
再親手把它收回去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業展、成果展、畢業製作撤展那天發；配一張空牆或捲起來的作品照最有感
variations: 貼了三個晚上，撕下來十一分鐘。這大概就是大學四年的比例。
作品可以捲起來帶走，那面牆帶不走，所以我拍了一張。

en.content:
Last day of the senior show. Doors close at five.

At 5:05
we started pulling everything off the wall.

That wall took us three nights.
We used a level. We measured the gaps.
One piece hung two millimeters crooked
and we redid it four times.

It came down in eleven minutes.

I rolled my work into a tube,
tucked it under my arm,
and looked back on the way out.

Our wall was just a white wall again.

Next week's group moves in.

So that's what finishing means:
you make the thing,
then you take it down yourself.
en.editorNote: For teardown day at a senior show, thesis exhibition, or capstone showcase — pairs well with a photo of the empty wall
variations: Three nights to hang. Eleven minutes to take down. That's roughly the ratio of college.
The work rolls up and comes with me. The wall doesn't, so I took a picture of it.

items.sourceNote: posts about quitting the campus-adjacent part-time job worked all through college, and the last shift before graduating

zh-tw.content:
校門口那家店，我打了三年工。

畢業前最後一班，
我以為店長會講幾句話。

他什麼都沒說。
只是走去看板前面，
把下禮拜班表上我的名字
用立可白塗掉。

塗得很慢，
塗完還吹了兩下。

打烊的時候他多裝了一份給我，
袋子遞過來的時候說：
「以後回來，我還是算你學生價。」

我在騎樓站了一下才走。

有些人不會跟你說再見，
他們用別的方式讓你知道
這裡永遠留著你的位子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合大學打工最後一班、或跟待了很久的店家、老闆道別時發；也適合傳給還在原地上班的同事
variations: 他沒說再見，只是把班表上的名字慢慢塗掉。
三年的班表少了一行，換來一句「回來還是算你學生價」。

en.content:
The place by the campus gate. I worked there three years.

Last shift before graduation.
I figured the manager would say something.

He didn't.
He just walked over to the board
and whited out my name
on next week's schedule.

Slowly. Then blew on it twice.

At close he packed me an extra order,
handed it over, and said:
"Come back anytime. Still your student price."

I stood outside for a minute before I left.

Some people don't say goodbye.
They find another way to tell you
your spot is still here.
en.editorNote: For your last shift at the job you kept all through college, or saying goodbye to a place you were a regular at
variations: He never said goodbye. He just took his time whiting my name off the schedule.
Three years of shifts, one line erased, and a standing student discount.

items.sourceNote: new-hire onboarding guides and first-week posts about being issued an employee number and access badge

zh-tw.content:
報到第一天，人事給我一組員工編號。

八碼。
她說登入系統、報帳、訂便當都要用。

我寫在便條紙上貼在螢幕下面，
貼了兩個禮拜，還是要看一眼。

可是我的學號，
十位數，四年前背起來的，
到現在還能倒著念。

沒有人教過我要背它，
它就是印在證件上、
寫在每一份考卷的右上角、
被同學喊過幾百次。

背久了就變成名字的一部分。

新的編號可能也會有那一天。
只是現在還不熟，
像剛搬進去的房子，
燈的開關在哪裡都還要找。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職前兩週發，講一組新數字取代舊數字那種不習慣；配便條紙或門禁卡照片很搭
variations: 學號背了四年不用想，員工編號兩個禮拜還要偷看便條紙。
換身分最實際的證據，是你要重新背一組數字。

en.content:
Day one. HR hands me an employee number.

Eight digits.
For the login, for expenses, for ordering lunch.

I wrote it on a sticky note under my monitor.
Two weeks in, I still glance at it.

Meanwhile my student ID number —
ten digits, memorized four years ago —
I can still say backwards.

Nobody told me to learn it.
It was just printed on the card,
written in the corner of every exam,
called out loud a few hundred times.

Eventually it became part of my name.

Maybe this one gets there too.
Right now it's still new,
like a place you just moved into
where you're still hunting for the light switch.
en.editorNote: For your first two weeks on the job — the strangeness of one set of digits replacing another. Pairs with a sticky note or badge photo
variations: Four years of student ID, no thinking required. Two weeks of employee number, still peeking at the sticky note.
The most concrete proof you changed identities: you have to memorize a new number.

items.sourceNote: student-org handover posts about passing on the club room key and clearing out things left by earlier cohorts

zh-tw.content:
交接那天，我把社辦鑰匙交出去。

交之前先整理。

抽屜最裡面翻到一個鐵盒，
裡面是三屆以前留下來的東西：
一支沒水的白板筆、
半包受潮的仙貝、
還有一張紙條寫著
「器材櫃鑰匙在盆栽下面，別跟老師講」。

那個盆栽早就死了。
寫紙條的人我根本不認識。

我把紙條放回去，
盒子關上，
塞回抽屜最裡面。

然後跟學妹說：
「這格不用整理。」

有些東西不是留給我的，
是留給這個空間的。
我只是剛好經過，
順便幫它傳下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合社團交接、卸任、把社辦或工作交給下一屆的時候發；也適合寫在給接任者的卡片裡
variations: 我不認識寫紙條的人，但我幫他把紙條留下來了。
交接交的不是鑰匙，是那個抽屜最裡面、誰都沒丟掉的盒子。

en.content:
Handover day. I gave up the club room key.

Cleaned it out first.

In the back of a drawer, a tin box
with stuff from three cohorts ago:
a dried-out whiteboard marker,
half a bag of stale rice crackers,
and a note that said
"equipment key is under the plant, don't tell the advisor."

The plant died years ago.
I have no idea who wrote the note.

I put it back,
closed the box,
and pushed it to the back of the drawer.

Then I told the new officer:
"Leave that drawer alone."

Some things aren't left for you.
They're left for the room.
You just pass through
and keep them moving.
en.editorNote: For club handovers and stepping down — passing a space, a role, or a key to whoever comes next. Works in a card to your successor
variations: I never met whoever wrote that note. I kept it anyway.
A handover isn't the key. It's the box at the back of the drawer nobody ever threw out.

items.sourceNote: campus wi-fi login threads — phones auto-reconnecting to school networks and accounts failing authentication after the student leaves

zh-tw.content:
回南部之前，我在學校那站轉車。

手機震了一下，
跳出一行通知：
已連線到校園無線網路。

它自己連上的。
密碼是四年前存的，
我早就忘了長什麼樣子。

瀏覽器跳出登入頁，
我輸入學號，
系統回我：查無此使用者。

網路還記得我這台手機，
系統已經把我刪掉了。

我點了「忘記此網路」。

點之前停了三秒。

不是捨不得那個網路，
是那是我身上最後一樣
還連著那裡的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業一段時間後，經過學校附近、手機自己連上舊校網的那一刻發；也適合當成清手機時的深夜限動
variations: 密碼還存在我手機裡，學號已經不存在系統裡了。
原來刪掉一個 Wi-Fi，也可以算一次告別。

en.content:
Campus Wi-Fi connected on its own while I was changing buses near school.

My phone still had the password. Saved four years ago. I couldn't tell you what it was.

The login page opened. I typed my student ID.

User not found.

The network still recognizes my phone. The system already deleted me.

I tapped "Forget This Network."

Then I sat there three seconds before I did it.

Not because I wanted the Wi-Fi back. It was just the last thing I had that was still connected to that place.
en.editorNote: For the moment your phone auto-joins your old campus network months after you left. Also works as a late-night caption while clearing out your phone
variations: My phone kept the password. The system didn't keep me.
Deleting a saved Wi-Fi network turned out to be a goodbye.

items.sourceNote: posts about longtime local eateries closing and the meals friends kept postponing until it was too late

zh-tw.content:
我們講了三年要一起去的那家店，
上個月門口貼了一張紅紙。

「感謝各位老顧客，本店結束營業。」

我們沒有吵架，也沒有絕交。
只是每次都說「下次」。

「下次」很便宜，
講出來不用付出任何東西。

那個位置現在是一間手搖店。

昨天我在群組傳了三個日期，
沒有問「大家什麼時候有空」，
直接問「哪一天不行」。

十分鐘內收到五個回覆。

原來不是大家都沒空，
是沒有人願意先講出一個日期。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合真的要把那頓拖很久的飯約成的時候發在群組裡；也適合看到常去的老店收掉、突然很想聯絡大學朋友的晚上
variations: 別再問「大家什麼時候有空」，改問「哪一天不行」，成功率差很多。
「下次」是全世界最便宜的承諾，因為它從來不用寫日期。

en.content:
Three years of saying we'd go to that place together. Last month a notice went up on the door.

Thanks for the years, we're closing.

Nobody fell out. Nobody stopped talking. We just kept saying "next time."

"Next time" is cheap. Saying it costs you nothing.

There's a bubble tea shop there now.

Yesterday I dropped three dates in the group chat. I didn't ask when everyone was free. I asked which day doesn't work.

Five replies in ten minutes.

Nobody was short on time. Everyone was just waiting for someone else to name a day.
en.editorNote: For when you're finally locking in the reunion dinner everyone keeps postponing — or the night your old spot closes and you want to text the group
variations: Stop asking when everyone's free. Ask which day doesn't work. The reply rate changes.
"Next time" is the cheapest promise there is. It never comes with a date.

items.sourceNote: workplace humor about file naming habits carried over from school assignments

zh-tw.content:
我畢業專題的資料夾長這樣：

期末報告_最終版
期末報告_最終版2
期末報告_真的最終版
期末報告_這次真的_交這個

出社會之後我以為會改掉。

沒有。

只是把「期末報告」
換成「提案」，
後面那一串一字不差。

四年沒有白念。
至少有一個技能，
我完整地帶出來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜改到第七版簡報、回頭看到自己資料夾裡一整排「最終版」的時候發
variations: 檔名裡出現「真的」兩個字，通常代表後面還有兩版。
課本內容忘了一半，命名習慣倒是一個字都沒改。

en.content:
Final_v2. Final_REAL. Final_REAL_send_this_one.

That was my senior project folder.

I assumed a real job would fix this.

It did not. I swapped "term paper" for "client deck" and left everything after the underscore exactly as it was.

Four years of school. This is the skill that made it out with me.
en.editorNote: For the 1 a.m. seventh revision, when you scroll up and see the whole column of files named final
variations: Any filename containing the word REAL has at least two versions after it.
I forgot half the coursework. The naming habit survived intact.

items.sourceNote: family posts about parents framing or laminating a grown child's diploma and hanging it in the living room

zh-tw.content:
回家那天，畢業證書我隨手擱在餐桌上。

隔兩個禮拜再回去，
它已經被護貝過，
掛在客廳電視旁邊那面牆上，
高度大概到我肩膀。

我說會不會太誇張，拿下來啦。

我媽在廚房，頭也沒回：

「那張是我的，不是你的。」

我愣了一下。

那張紙上印的是我的名字，
可是四年的學費、
每個月匯過來的生活費、
還有她從來沒講出口的擔心，
一個字都沒有印在上面。

它現在掛的位置，
剛好是她每天煮完飯
一抬頭就看得到的地方。

好，那就掛著吧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回家發現爸媽把你的證書掛起來的那天發；也適合想謝家人卻講不出口、只好寫在限動裡的時候
variations: 證書上印的是我的名字，真正付出去的那些東西一項都沒印上去。
我說拿下來啦。我媽說：那張是我的。

en.content:
Diploma sat on the dining table where I dropped it when I got home.

Two weeks later I visited again. It was laminated and hanging in the living room next to the TV, about shoulder height.

I said that's a bit much, take it down.

Mom didn't turn around from the kitchen. "That one's mine, not yours."

My name is the thing printed on it. The tuition, the money wired over every month, and all the worrying she never mentioned are not.

It hangs exactly where she looks up after cooking.

Fine. Leave it there.
en.editorNote: For the day you go home and find your parents put your diploma on the wall, or when you want to thank family and can't say it out loud
variations: My name is printed on it. Everything that actually paid for it isn't.
I told her to take it down. She said it wasn't mine to take down.

items.sourceNote: university graduation clearance procedures requiring sign-off from library, dorm, department office and bursar before the diploma is released

zh-tw.content:
領畢業證書之前，
要先跑一張單子。

圖書館一個章：確認你沒欠書。
宿舍一個章：確認你沒留東西。
系辦一個章：確認你沒欠學分。
出納組一個章：確認你沒欠錢。

集滿了，才換得到那張紙。

我跑了整整一個下午，
跑到最後忽然發現一件事——

每一格問的都是
「你有沒有欠學校」，

沒有一格問
「你有沒有帶走什麼」。

那一格沒有人蓋，
只能自己填。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合跑完離校手續、當天拿到證書時發；也適合想寫「畢業其實是一連串行政流程」的貼文
variations: 離校單上每一格都在問我欠學校什麼，沒有一格問我學到了什麼。
四年的最後一份作業，是集章。

en.content:
