Before they hand over the diploma, you have to run a clearance sheet.

Stamp from the library: you don't owe any books.
Stamp from the dorm: you didn't leave anything behind.
Stamp from the department office: you don't owe any credits.
Stamp from the bursar: you don't owe any money.

Collect them all and you can trade them for the paper.

It took me a whole afternoon, and somewhere near the end it hit me.

Every box asks what I still owe the school.

Not one box asks what I'm taking with me.

Nobody stamps that one. You fill it in yourself.
en.editorNote: For the day you finish your graduation clearance and pick up the diploma, or a post about graduation being mostly paperwork
variations: Every box on the clearance form asked what I owed. None asked what I learned.
The final assignment of four years was collecting stamps.

items.sourceNote: forum threads from admitted grad students about the limbo summer between commencement and orientation

zh-tw.content:
我這個暑假的正式身分是「碩零」。

畢業了，但還沒開學。
不是學生，也不是上班族。
舊的學生證繳回去了，
新的還沒發下來。

親戚問我在幹嘛，
我說在讀書。
他們問讀什麼，
我說還沒開始。

同學的動態一個接一個
變成「到職第一天」，
我的是「九月三號報到」。

別人畢業是離開學校，
我畢業是續約。

差別在於——
這次的合約是我自己簽的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合考上研究所、卡在畢業與開學之間的暑假發；也適合回答親戚那句「你怎麼還在讀書」
variations: 不是學生也不是上班族，我目前的身分是「碩零」。
別人畢業是離開學校，我畢業是續約，而且是自己簽的。

en.content:
My official status this summer is "year zero."

Graduated, not yet enrolled. Not a student, not an employee. Turned in the old ID card, the new one isn't printed yet.

Relatives ask what I'm doing. I say studying. They ask what. I say it hasn't started.

My classmates' feeds keep turning into "first day at work." Mine says orientation, September 3.

For everyone else, graduating means leaving school. For me it means renewing.

The difference is that this time I signed the contract myself.
en.editorNote: For anyone stuck between commencement and grad school orientation, or fielding "wait, you're still in school?"
variations: Not a student, not an employee. Current status: year zero.
Everyone else left school. I renewed, and this time I signed it myself.

items.sourceNote: posts about scraping campus parking permits and other school stickers off a scooter after graduating

zh-tw.content:
我把機車上那張學校停車證撕掉了。

貼了四年，撕下來只掉一半，
剩下的用指甲刮、用去漬油擦，
最後還是留下一塊比較白的方形。

車行的人說，這個很難弄乾淨。
我說沒關係。

那塊白的形狀，
跟停車證一模一樣。

它每天早上八點，
停在系館後面那排的第三格。

現在它跟我一起停在
公司樓下的月租車位，
一個月一千二。

沒有人知道那塊白色是什麼。

只有我知道。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合騎車通勤、剛換到新生活的人發；也適合寫「有些痕跡撕不掉」的懷舊貼文
variations: 停車證撕掉了，留下一塊比較白的方形，形狀跟它一模一樣。
沒有人知道那塊白色是什麼，只有我知道。

en.content:
I peeled the campus parking permit off my scooter.

Four years of adhesive. Half came away, the rest took a fingernail and some solvent, and it still left a paler square behind.

The shop guy said that kind never comes off clean. I said it's fine.

The pale square is exactly the shape of the permit.

At eight every morning, that permit sat in the third slot of the row behind the department building.

Now it parks with me in a monthly space under the office. Twelve hundred a month.

Nobody knows what that pale square is.

I do.
en.editorNote: For anyone who commutes by scooter into a brand-new life, or a post about the marks that don't scrub off
variations: The permit came off. The paler square it left is exactly its shape.
Nobody knows what that pale square is. I do.

items.sourceNote: posts about visiting a former professor after graduation and being told to drop the title

zh-tw.content:
畢業之後第一次回系上，
我去敲了教授的門。

還是那個角落，
門上還是那張泛黃的公告。

他倒了茶，問我工作怎麼樣。
我講到一半，
下意識接了一句：

「老師，那個報告我……」

他笑了：
「你不用交報告了。
而且以後可以直接叫我名字。」

我點頭。

然後下一句還是脫口而出——

「老師。」

有些稱呼改不掉。
不是因為習慣，
是因為那四年，
真的有人這樣教過你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後回學校看老師的那天發；也適合想謝謝某位老師卻不知道怎麼開口的時候
variations: 他說以後可以叫他名字，我點頭，下一句還是叫了老師。
有些稱呼改不掉，因為那四年真的有人這樣教過你。

en.content:
First time back at the department after graduating, I knocked on my professor's door.

Same corner office. Same yellowed notice taped to it.

He poured tea and asked how work was going. Halfway through my answer I heard myself say, "Professor, about that paper, I—"

He laughed. "You don't turn in papers anymore. And you can use my first name now."

I nodded.

The next sentence out of my mouth still started with "Professor."

Some titles don't come off. Not out of habit. Because for four years somebody actually earned it.
en.editorNote: For the day you go back to campus to visit a teacher, or when you want to thank one and can't find the opening
variations: He told me to use his first name. I nodded, then said Professor again.
Some titles don't come off — for four years somebody actually earned it.

items.sourceNote: posts about student-rate subscriptions auto-converting to full price once enrollment ends

zh-tw.content:
這個月的扣款怎麼變兩倍？

翻到信箱最下面，
一封三天前的通知：

「您的學生方案已到期，
系統偵測到在學身分失效，
將自動轉為一般方案。」

畢業典禮上講了那麼多祝福，
最後是這封信
說得最直白：

同學，你不是學生了。

好吧。
從今天起，
每一塊錢都是我自己的價錢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合學生優惠被系統默默收回那天發限動；也適合傳給還剩最後一年學生身分的學弟妹
variations: 畢業典禮講了那麼多祝福，最後是漲價通知講得最直白。
從今天起，每一塊錢都是我自己的價錢。

en.content:
Why did this month's charge double?

Buried at the bottom of my inbox, a notice from three days ago:

"Your student plan has expired. Our records show you are no longer enrolled. Your account will convert to the standard rate."

All those speeches at commencement, and this billing email said it plainest of all:

You're not a student anymore.

Fine.
From today, every price I pay is my own price.
en.editorNote: For the day a student discount quietly turns into full price, or to send to a friend on their last year of eligibility
variations: Commencement had the speeches. The billing email had the truth.
From today, every price I pay is my own price.

items.sourceNote: posts about alumni fundraising calls arriving only weeks after commencement

zh-tw.content:
畢業第二個月，學校打電話來。

不是通知我學分沒過，
也不是問我證書領了沒。

是很客氣地說：
「親愛的校友，
我們正在募款蓋新的活動中心。」

校友。
第一次有人這樣叫我。

我坐在租來的套房裡，
用著公司借我的筆電，
存款只有三位數，
卻被叫得像個有頭有臉的人。

我說我現在只捐得起祝福。
對方笑著說，那也算。

掛掉電話我愣了一下——
原來我已經被歸到
「被學校期待」的那一邊了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合第一次被叫「校友」的那天發；也適合寫給還沒站穩、卻已經被當成大人的自己
variations: 第一次被叫校友，是在一通募款電話裡。
存款三位數，卻被叫得像個有頭有臉的人。

en.content:
Second month out, the school called.

Not about a missing credit. Not about picking up my diploma.

Just a very polite voice: "Dear alum, we're raising funds for the new student center."

Alum.
First time anyone had called me that.

I was sitting in a rented room, on a laptop my company loaned me, three digits in my bank account, being addressed like somebody important.

I said the only thing I could donate right now was goodwill. She laughed and said that counts.

After I hung up it landed on me: I'm on the other side now. The side the school expects things from.
en.editorNote: For the first time someone calls you an alum, or for anyone being treated like an adult before they feel like one
variations: First time anyone called me an alum, it was a fundraising call.
Three digits in the bank, addressed like somebody important.

items.sourceNote: new-grad interview threads about being asked why you chose your major

zh-tw.content:
面試官問：
「當初為什麼選這個科系？」

老實說，
十八歲那年是分數帶我來的。
那時候我連系上在教什麼
都說不清楚。

但我開口講的是大三那個專題，
講那門課讓我第一次
熬夜熬得心甘情願。

走出會議室我才想通：
兩個答案都是真的。

把我放進來的不是我，
但把它變成我的，
是我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合面試前給自己看；也適合任何覺得自己是「誤打誤撞走進這一行」的人
variations: 十八歲那年是分數帶我來的，但把它變成我的是我。
誤打誤撞走進來，四年之後是我自己決定要留下。

en.content:
The interviewer asked, "So why did you pick this major?"

Honestly? At eighteen, my test scores picked it. I couldn't have told you what the department actually taught.

But what came out of my mouth was the junior-year project, and the one class that made staying up all night feel like a choice.

Walking out, I realized both answers are true.

Something else put me in that room. Making it mine was all me.
en.editorNote: Read it before an interview, or on any day you feel like you landed in your field by accident
variations: My test scores picked the major. I'm the one who made it mine.
I got there by accident. Staying was my call.

items.sourceNote: posts about losing campus health center access and handling being sick alone after graduating

zh-tw.content:
以前不舒服，
走幾步就到健康中心，
刷個學生證、量個體溫，
護理師還會順手
給我一張請假證明。

現在我發燒，
自己查診所、自己掛號、
自己坐在候診區等叫號。

沒有人幫我寫假單，
也沒有人問我為什麼沒到。

原來長大就是這麼一回事：
生不生病是身體的事，
照顧自己變成你的事。

所以好好吃飯、早點睡。
從今天起，
你就是自己的校護。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後第一次自己看醫生的那天；也適合傳給一個人在外地、生病沒人知道的朋友
variations: 沒有人幫你寫假單了，也沒有人問你為什麼沒到。
從今天起，你就是自己的校護。

en.content:
Feeling lousy used to mean a two-minute walk to the campus health center. Flash a student ID, get your temperature taken, leave with a signed note excusing you from class.

Now I run a fever and I look up clinics myself, check in myself, sit in the waiting room myself watching the numbers tick.

Nobody writes me a note. Nobody asks why I wasn't there.

Turns out that's the whole trick of growing up: getting sick is your body's business, taking care of yourself becomes yours.

So eat something. Sleep early. As of today, you're your own school nurse.
en.editorNote: For the first time you see a doctor on your own after graduating, or for a friend living alone with nobody to tell they're sick
variations: Nobody writes you a note anymore. Nobody asks why you weren't there.
As of today, you're your own school nurse.

items.sourceNote: threads where people remember classroom details years later far better than any course material

zh-tw.content:
畢業八年，
高中三年的課本內容
我一句都背不出來。

但你現在問我座位表，
我可以畫給你。

窗邊第三個位子是誰的、
冷氣正下方多搶手、
誰的椅子一直在晃，
底下墊了一疊考卷。

原來我讀的不是那間學校，
是坐在我旁邊的那些人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合同學會前一天丟出來當開場；也適合某天路過母校、突然想起自己坐哪一排的時候
variations: 課本一句都背不出來，座位表倒是可以畫給你。
我讀的不是那間學校，是坐在我旁邊的那些人。

en.content:
Eight years out, I can't quote one line from any textbook I owned in high school.

Ask for the seating chart, though, and I'll draw it. Third desk by the window. The spot directly under the air conditioner, most contested real estate in the building. The chair that wobbled, propped up with a folded stack of old exams.

Turns out I didn't attend that school. I attended the people sitting around me.
en.editorNote: Good opener for the group thread before a reunion, or for the day you drive past your old school and remember your exact row
variations: Can't quote the textbook. Can draw the seating chart.
I didn't attend that school. I attended the people around me.

items.sourceNote: posts about finding old school uniforms while clearing out a childhood bedroom

zh-tw.content:
回老家整理房間，
在衣櫃最裡面翻到那件制服。

洗到有點透，
領口起了毛，
但摺線還在，
像是誰認真收好的。

我試著穿，
肩膀卡住了。

這件衣服這幾年沒有動過，
是我自己長開了。

「你變了」這三個字
通常不是稱讚。
只有這一次，
它是好消息。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回老家翻舊東西的那個下午；也適合傳給正在懷疑自己這幾年到底有沒有長進的朋友
variations: 這件衣服這幾年沒有動過，是我自己長開了。
「你變了」通常不是稱讚，只有這一次是好消息。

en.content:
Cleaning out my childhood room, I found it shoved at the back of the closet. Old school uniform, washed thin, collar gone fuzzy, still folded along the same creases like somebody put it away on purpose.

Tried it on. Shoulders wouldn't go.

The shirt hasn't moved in years. I'm the thing that grew.

"You've changed" is almost never a compliment. This one time, it's good news.
en.editorNote: For the afternoon you dig through old boxes at your parents' place, or a friend wondering whether they've actually grown at all
variations: The shirt hasn't moved in years. I'm the thing that grew.
"You've changed" is almost never a compliment. This once, it is.

items.sourceNote: discussions comparing school cleaning-duty rotations with keeping your own place tidy after moving out

zh-tw.content:
學校最被低估的制度
是打掃時間。

每天固定十五分鐘，
全校一起，
有人負責掃、有人負責倒，
有人負責站著監督，
時間到了自然就結束。

出社會之後才發現，
再也沒有人幫我排班了。

我家的地板
上一次被拖是什麼時候，
沒有紀錄，
也不會有人來檢查。

原來那張輪值表
不是在管你，
是在替你決定：
今天這件事，做完了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人住、家裡開始慢慢失守的時候；也適合傳給剛搬出來、還在跟自己談判要不要拖地的朋友
variations: 出社會之後才發現，再也沒有人幫我排班了。
那張輪值表不是在管你，是在替你決定今天這件事做完了。

en.content:
Fifteen minutes a day, whole school at once. Cleaning time was the most underrated system I have ever been enrolled in. Somebody swept, somebody hauled the trash, somebody stood there supervising, and when the bell went the job was over.

Nobody puts me on a rotation anymore.

The last time my floor got mopped is recorded nowhere, and nobody is coming to check.

Turns out that duty roster wasn't there to boss you around. It was there to decide, on your behalf, that today this thing was finished.
en.editorNote: For anyone living alone whose apartment is quietly sliding, or a friend who just moved out and keeps negotiating with themselves about the floor
variations: Nobody puts me on a cleaning rotation anymore.
The roster wasn't bossing you around. It was deciding the day was done.

items.sourceNote: Dcard mood-board thread on whether to attend a high school reunion after starting work

zh-tw.content:
同學會的前三十分鐘，
大家都在報職稱。

在哪家公司、做什麼的、
最近忙不忙。
語速很平、笑點很少，
像在開一場沒有主題的會。

第三十一分鐘，
有人提起某年朝會誰昏倒，
誰的情書送到隔壁班。

職稱就這樣全部失效了。

後面那兩個小時，
沒有人再問誰過得比較好，
只有人一直說：
「你以前根本不是這樣。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合同學會前一天先丟出來降低大家的壓力；也適合說服那個怕自己「拿不出東西」而不想去的朋友
variations: 同學會的前三十分鐘在報職稱，第三十一分鐘全部失效。
沒有人再問誰過得比較好，只有人一直說「你以前根本不是這樣」。

en.content:
First thirty minutes of any reunion are job titles. Which company, what department, how busy things have been. Flat delivery, almost no laughing, like a meeting nobody set an agenda for.

Minute thirty-one, somebody brings up the kid who fainted at morning assembly, and the love letter that got delivered to the wrong classroom.

Every job title expires on the spot.

The two hours after that, nobody asks who's doing better. People just keep saying, "You were absolutely not like this before."
en.editorNote: Send it to the group the night before a reunion, or to the friend skipping it because they think they have nothing to show
variations: Thirty minutes of job titles. Then they all expire.
Nobody asks who's doing better. They just say you were not like this before.

items.sourceNote: Dcard military board thread debating whether to shave your head before reporting for service

zh-tw.content:
入伍前一天，我去剃頭。

設計師問：「要多短？」
我說：「最短的那個。」

她點點頭，換了一支推剪，
說這個夏天她剃到會背役期了。

鏡子裡的頭髮一撮一撮往下掉。
剃到一半她補了一句：
「你知道進去還是會再剃一次吧？」

我說知道。

「那你今天是剃心安的。」

走出店門，
風第一次吹到我的後腦勺。

畢業典禮沒讓我有實感的那件事，
一支推剪就辦到了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合入伍前一晚發限動；也適合傳給那個明天要去剃頭、嘴上一直說「還好啊」的朋友
variations: 「你知道進去還是會再剃一次吧？」「知道。」「那你今天是剃心安的。」
畢業典禮沒讓我有實感的那件事，一支推剪就辦到了。

en.content:
Day before I report for service, I go get my head shaved.

"How short?" the stylist asks.
"Shortest setting you've got."

She nods, swaps in a different clipper, says she's done so many heads this summer she could recite the service calendar from memory.

Hair comes off in clumps. Halfway through she adds, "You know they'll just shave it again once you're inside, right?"

I know.

"So today's the one for peace of mind."

Out on the street, wind hits the back of my head for the first time.

The ceremony never made it feel real. A pair of clippers did.
en.editorNote: For the night before you report, or for the friend insisting the haircut is no big deal
variations: "You know they'll shave it again inside, right?" "I know." "So today's the one for peace of mind."
The ceremony never made it feel real. A pair of clippers did.

items.sourceNote: Dcard mood-board thread on adulthood getting harder; used as the seed for the college-August vs working-August contrast

zh-tw.content:
八月一直是我的待辦清單月。

大學四年的八月：
查課表、
問學長哪個老師好過、
算學分還差幾、
找同學湊一門通識。

今年八月：
查勞健保到底怎麼扣、
問前輩哪家牙醫不用等、
算薪水扣完剩多少、
找房仲湊一個住得下的坪數。

一樣是挑，一樣是算。

差別只在，
這次沒有加簽單可以救，
也沒有人可以問「這個甜不甜」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學季看著學弟妹在搶課、自己已經不在名單上時發；也適合當第一份工作滿一個月的自嘲貼文
variations: 大學的八月在算學分，出社會的八月在算薪水扣完剩多少。
一樣是挑，一樣是算，只是這次沒有加簽單可以救。

en.content:
August has always been my to-do list month.

August, all four years of college:
check the timetable,
ask an upperclassman which professor grades easy,
count how many credits I'm still short,
find someone to take a filler course with.

August this year:
check what actually gets deducted for insurance,
ask a senior coworker which dentist doesn't make you wait,
count what's left of the paycheck after everything,
find a place with enough square footage to live in.

Same picking. Same math.

The only difference is there's no add-drop form to save me now, and nobody to ask whether this one is an easy A.
en.editorNote: Post it when the semester starts and you're not in it, or a month into the first job
variations: In college, August meant counting credits. Now it means counting what's left of the paycheck.
Same picking, same math. Just no add-drop form to save me.

items.sourceNote: Dcard mood-board thread about no longer having your own room at your parents' place

zh-tw.content:
畢業後第一次回家住幾天，
推開房門，書桌是空的。

參考書收進紙箱疊在陽台，
角落多了一張瑜珈墊、
一台除濕機，
還有一盆被照顧得很好的植物。

我媽在門口說：
「東西我沒丟，都在陽台。
反正你也不常回來。」

語氣很平，不是在酸我。

衣櫃她留了一半沒動，
床單還是我高中挑的那組。

我在門口看了一圈才想通——

不是她把我趕出去，
是我空出來的那些地方，
她終於拿去過自己的日子了。

那年畢業的，
不只我一個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在回老家的照片旁邊；也適合傳給那個嘴上抱怨房間被改造、其實心裡有點空的朋友
variations: 不是她把我趕出去，是我空出來的地方，她終於拿去過自己的日子了。
那年畢業的，不只我一個。

en.content:
First time home for a few days since graduating. I push the door open and the desk is bare.

My textbooks are boxed up and stacked on the balcony. In the corner there's a yoga mat now, a dehumidifier, and a plant that is very obviously being looked after.

Mom, from the doorway: "I didn't throw anything out, it's all on the balcony. You're barely here anyway."

Flat delivery. Not a dig.

She left half the closet untouched. The sheets are still the ones I picked out in high school.

Took me one slow look around the room to get it.

She didn't push me out. The space I stopped using, she finally took back for her own life.

I wasn't the only one who graduated that year.
en.editorNote: Caption for a photo from a trip home, or for the friend complaining their old room got repurposed
variations: She didn't push me out. The space I stopped using, she took back for her own life.
I wasn't the only one who graduated that year.

items.sourceNote: Dcard mood-board thread on going back to school places after graduating; seed for the first-tutoring-job angle

zh-tw.content:
畢業後第一筆收入，
是家教的鐘點費。

學生卡在一題數學，
我講到一半停住——

那句口訣不是我想出來的。
是我高中老師掛在嘴邊、
我當年嫌很煩的那一句。

我原封不動地傳下去了。

有些東西不用背，
它自己會走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合接第一份家教或打工時發；也適合教師節前後傳給以前的老師當開場白
variations: 我原封不動地把老師那句口訣傳下去了。
有些東西不用背，它自己會走。

en.content:
First money I made after graduating was hourly tutoring pay.

My student got stuck on a math problem, and halfway through the explanation I stopped.

The trick I was reciting wasn't mine. It was the one my high school teacher said constantly, the one I found unbearably annoying at the time.

I passed it on word for word.

Some things you never memorize. They walk over on their own.
en.editorNote: For your first tutoring gig after graduation, or as an opening line to an old teacher around Teachers' Day
variations: I passed my teacher's line on word for word without even noticing.
Some things you never memorize. They walk over on their own.

items.sourceNote: Dcard graduation board; seed is the school year restarting for everyone except you

zh-tw.content:
開學那週，
車廂裡制服又變多了。

同一班車、同一個時間，
只有我不是要去上學。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學前後通勤時發限動；也適合傳給第一次沒有開學可過的朋友
variations: 同一班車、同一個時間，只有我不是要去上學。
車廂裡制服又變多了，只是這次跟我沒關係。

en.content:
Semester restarts. My train car fills with uniforms again.

Same train, same time. I'm just the only one not going to school.
en.editorNote: For a commute post around the first week of term, or a friend with no semester to start
variations: Same train, same time. I'm just the only one not going to school.
The uniforms are back on my train. None of them are mine.

items.sourceNote: Dcard mood thread on missing student life; seed for the recurring unfinished-assignment dream

zh-tw.content:
畢業好幾年了，
還是會夢到有一份作業沒交。

醒來第一秒是慌，
第二秒有點想念。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被學生時期的夢驚醒時發；也適合回那個又夢到期末的朋友
variations: 醒來第一秒是慌，第二秒有點想念。
畢業好幾年，那份沒交的作業還在夢裡等我。

en.content:
Years out, and I still dream about an assignment I never turned in.

First second awake, panic. Second second, I kind of miss it.
en.editorNote: For the morning after a school anxiety dream, or a friend who dreamed about finals again
variations: First second awake, panic. Second second, I kind of miss it.
Years out, and that assignment I never turned in still waits for me in dreams.

items.sourceNote: essay on why adult friendships need calendar coordination; reframed for post-graduation classmates

zh-tw.content:
以前見面不用約。
走到教室後排，你就在。

現在要先問哪天有空，
再對兩個行事曆，
最後訂在三個禮拜後的星期六。

我們沒有變壞，
只是從「本來就在」
變成「要挪出來」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合終於約成那頓飯的當天發；也適合傳給那個一直說「再約」的朋友
variations: 以前見面不用約，走到教室後排，你就在。
我們沒有變壞，只是從「本來就在」變成「要挪出來」。

en.content:
We never used to make plans. I walked to the back row and you were there.

Now it's which day works, then two calendars side by side, then a Saturday three weeks out.

Nothing went wrong between us. We just went from already there to has to be carved out.
en.editorNote: For the day a long-postponed dinner finally happens, or the friend who keeps saying let's catch up sometime
variations: We never used to make plans. I walked to the back row and you were there.
Nothing went wrong. We just went from already there to has to be carved out.

items.sourceNote: Dcard job-board thread looking back two years after graduating; seed for the pronoun that never updated

zh-tw.content:
同事問我哪畢業的。
我報了學校名字，
接著補一句：「我們學校在山上，冬天很冷。」

說完自己愣了一下。

畢業三年，
那兩個字還沒改口。

離開一個地方很快，
把它從「我們」裡拿掉，
慢很多。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊到學校時被自己的用詞戳到；也適合當簡短的自我介紹貼文
variations: 離開一個地方很快，把它從「我們」裡拿掉，慢很多。
畢業三年，「我們學校」那兩個字還沒改口。

en.content:
A coworker asked where I went to school. I said the name, then added, "Our campus is up in the mountains, it gets freezing."

Caught myself right after.

Three years out and the word our still hasn't updated.

Leaving a place is fast. Getting it out of "our" takes a lot longer.
en.editorNote: For the moment your own wording catches you off guard, or a short intro post
variations: Leaving a place is fast. Getting it out of "our" takes a lot longer.
Three years out and the word "our" still hasn't updated.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後第一個八月，班級群組停止更新的體感；原創短句

zh-tw.content: 群組往上滑，最後一則停在領畢業證書那天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合八月翻到舊群組時發限動，配一張只有日期的截圖
variations: 群組沒有解散，只是日期不再往前走。
最後一則訊息，是那天說的「等等在校門口集合」。

en.content: Scrolled up in the group chat. The last message is still from the day we picked up our diplomas.
en.editorNote: For an August story post, paired with a screenshot showing only the date
variations: Nobody left the group chat. The date just stopped moving.
Last message in there: "meet at the front gate in five."

items.sourceNote: 八月開學採買季與畢業生無關的失落感；原創短句

zh-tw.content: 開學特賣的牌子掛出來了。今年沒有一樣東西是我要買的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合八月路過文具店或賣場時發，配貨架照片
variations: 路過開學特賣，第一次覺得那些字不是在跟我說話。
以前八月要買新的，今年八月只剩下舊的。

en.content: The back-to-school sale signs are up. This year not a single item on them is mine to buy.
en.editorNote: For walking past a stationery aisle in August, with a shelf photo
variations: Walked past the back-to-school aisle and realized none of it was addressed to me.
August used to mean buying new things. Now it just means keeping the old ones.

items.sourceNote: 想在安靜的群組說話卻找不到理由的猶豫；原創短句

zh-tw.content: 在群組打了一個「欸」，又刪掉。想不到後面要接什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜想聯絡老同學卻按不下送出時發；也適合傳給同樣安靜的那個人
variations: 不是沒話說，是沒有事情可以當理由。
以前開口不用理由，現在要先想一個。

en.content: Typed "hey" in the group chat, then deleted it. Couldn't think of what would come after.
en.editorNote: For the late-night urge to message old classmates that never gets sent
variations: It's not that there's nothing to say. There's just no reason attached to it.
We used to talk without a reason. Now I have to invent one first.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後失去共同行程的空虛感，區分於單純的想念；原創短句

zh-tw.content: 八月的空，不是少了誰，是少了一個非見不可的日子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合解釋畢業後那種說不上來的空，配空教室或空月曆的照片
variations: 以前不用約，因為時間表會幫我們約。
大家都還在，只是不再被同一個日期叫到同一個地方。

en.content: August feels empty not because someone's missing, but because nothing on the calendar puts us in the same room anymore.
en.editorNote: For naming that vague post-grad emptiness, with an empty classroom or blank calendar photo
variations: We never had to make plans. The timetable made them for us.
Everyone's still around. Nothing schedules us into the same room now.

items.sourceNote: 新鮮人上工後失去外部方向感的討論；翻轉「被問志向很煩」的原創寫法

zh-tw.content:
從小到大，每隔一陣子就會有人問我：以後想做什麼？

國中問過，高中問過，大學面試也問過。
每次我都覺得很煩。

上班之後，這個問題突然不見了。
現在別人問的是這週進度到哪、下班要不要一起走。

我才發現那句煩死人的話，
其實是有人幫我
每年檢查一次方向。

現在沒人檢查了。
只能自己排一個時間，
坐下來問自己一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合出社會半年、覺得日子被進度填滿卻不知道往哪走的時候發；也適合傳給還在被親戚追問志向的學弟妹
variations: 以前嫌那個問題煩，現在才知道它是免費的年度健檢。
那句話沒有不見，只是從此以後只有我自己會講。

en.content:
Growing up, every couple of years somebody asked me: so what do you want to do?

Middle school asked. High school asked. The college interview asked.
Every time, I found it annoying.

Then I started working, and the question just vanished.
Now people ask how far along I am this week, or whether I'm walking out at six.

Turns out that annoying question
was somebody checking my direction
once a year, for free.

No one's checking now.
So I have to book the time myself,
sit down, and ask it out loud.
en.editorNote: For six months into the first job, when the calendar is full but the direction isn't
variations: I used to hate that question. It was a free annual checkup and I didn't know it.
The question didn't go away. It's just that I'm the only one who asks it now.

items.sourceNote: 上工三個月想離職的請益串；把大學加退選制度拿來對照職涯選擇的原創寫法

zh-tw.content:
如果工作也有加退選就好了。

前兩週先進去坐著聽，
覺得不對，在期限前按一下退選，
成績單乾乾淨淨，
沒人知道你來過。

可惜沒有。

現在每一個選擇都直接寫進正本，
而且找不到一個日期可以讓你反悔。

所以這次我花了比選課還久的時間，
才把送出按下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合猶豫要不要接 offer、或剛遞出離職單時發；配 offer 信或空白表單的截圖
variations: 學校讓你試兩週，職場要你先簽名。
沒有退選期，只好把猶豫全部花在按下去之前。

en.content:
I wish jobs had an add/drop period.

You'd sit in for two weeks, and if it felt wrong
you'd drop it before the deadline —
transcript clean, no trace you were ever there.

They don't.

Every choice goes straight onto the permanent record now,
and there's no date that lets you take it back.

So this time I spent longer than I ever spent picking courses
before I hit submit.
en.editorNote: For sitting on an offer, or the week you hand in your notice
variations: School gave you two weeks to try it. Work asks for the signature up front.
No drop deadline, so all the hesitating has to happen before you click.

items.sourceNote: 新人上班穿皮鞋磨腳的討論串；改寫為物件視角的成長比喻

zh-tw.content:
那雙皮鞋是我自己買的第一雙。

店員說皮的會鬆，建議我買大半號。我說好。

第一個禮拜，兩邊後跟都磨破，
抽屜裡放了一整排 OK 繃。
第三個禮拜還是痛，但至少知道痛在哪。

現在鞋跟外側被我走出一個斜斜的角度，
鞋面橫過腳背有一道摺痕。

它沒有變好看。

只是走到今天，
它終於只合我一個人的腳。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合上班滿兩三個月、發現自己好像撐下來了的時候發；配桌子底下或鞋櫃的那雙鞋
variations: 不是它自己變軟的，是我一天一天踩開的。
新的時候誰穿都可以，磨出形狀以後就只剩你穿得下。

en.content:
Those are the first dress shoes I ever bought myself.

The clerk said leather stretches, so I went half a size up. Sure, I said.

Week one, both heels were raw
and I kept a row of bandages in my desk drawer.
Week three still hurt, but at least I knew where.

Now the outer heels are worn to a slight angle,
and a crease runs across the top of my foot.

They don't look better.

They just, somewhere along the way,
stopped fitting anyone but me.
en.editorNote: For the two- or three-month mark at a first job, when you notice you made it through
variations: They didn't soften on their own. I walked them open, one day at a time.
Brand new, anyone could wear them. Broken in, only you can.

items.sourceNote: 社會新鮮人的一天作息討論；改寫為午休時間拆解的原創計算

zh-tw.content:
公司的午休是六十分鐘。

我算過：走出去七分鐘，排隊十一分鐘，
坐著吃二十二分鐘，
剩下的靠在椅背上，
連手機都不想解鎖。

一天八個小時裡，
只有那二十二分鐘
不需要我回應任何人。

中午不是拿來吃飯的。
是拿來把自己撿回來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合上班日中午發限動，配便當、空位子或走廊的照片
variations: 六十分鐘裡，真正屬於我的是二十二分鐘。
午休重要的不是吃什麼，是那段不用回話的時間。

en.content:
Lunch break here is sixty minutes.

I've timed it: seven to walk out, eleven in line,
twenty-two actually sitting and eating,
and the rest leaning back in the chair,
not even wanting to unlock my phone.

Out of eight hours,
those twenty-two minutes
are the only stretch where nobody needs an answer from me.

Lunch isn't for eating.
It's for getting yourself back.
en.editorNote: For a weekday noon story, paired with a lunchbox or an empty seat
variations: Sixty minutes on paper. Twenty-two of them are actually mine.
What matters at noon isn't the food. It's the stretch where no one needs a reply.

items.sourceNote: 颱風假的學生／上班族差異討論串；改寫為原創的宿舍與辦公室對照

zh-tw.content:
以前颱風要來的晚上，我可以撐到兩點還在刷市政府的公告。

「明日停班停課」四個字一出來，整層宿舍會先鬼吼一輪，然後有人衝去便利商店掃泡麵。

今年同一則通知跳出來，我第一個念頭是明天那場會要不要改線上。

我把手機蓋在桌上，鬧鐘照樣設七點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合颱風警報發布的那晚發限動，配窗外的雨或桌上的行事曆
variations: 同一則停班停課，以前是禮物，現在是行程調整通知。
我還是會刷公告。只是刷完要打開的是會議連結。

en.content:
A typhoon night used to mean staying up till two, refreshing the city government's page.

The second "classes canceled" appeared, the whole dorm floor would howl, and somebody would sprint out to clear the shelf of instant noodles.

This year the same alert popped up and my first thought was whether tomorrow's meeting moves online.

I put the phone face down. The alarm is still set for seven.
en.editorNote: For the night a storm warning drops, paired with rain on the window or a full calendar
variations: Same alert. It used to be a gift; now it's a scheduling problem.
I still refresh the announcement. I just open the meeting link right after.

items.sourceNote: 社會新鮮人第一份薪水的用途討論；改寫為原創的餐廳搶結帳場景

zh-tw.content:
第一份薪水入帳那週，我約我爸出來吃飯。

吃到一半他放下筷子說要去洗手間，我知道那是要去結帳，先一步把卡壓在櫃台上。

他走過來站在我後面，什麼都沒說，手還插在口袋裡。

回程車上他一路沒講幾句，下車前才丟一句：下次不用挑這麼貴的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合領到第一份薪水、請家人吃飯後發文，配餐廳桌面或收據
variations: 他讓我付了。那大概是最安靜的一次交接。
以前是他先站起來，現在換我先站起來。

en.content:
The week my first paycheck landed, I asked my dad out to dinner.

Halfway through he put down his chopsticks and said he was going to the restroom — I knew that meant the register, so I got there first and set my card on the counter.

He came up behind me and said nothing, hands still in his pockets.

He barely spoke on the drive home, and right before I got out he said: next time don't pick somewhere this expensive.
en.editorNote: For the first paycheck dinner with family, paired with a table shot or a receipt
variations: He let me pay. Quietest handover of my life.
He used to be the one who stood up first. Now it's me.

items.sourceNote: 「下定決心離職的瞬間」討論串；改寫為原創的同屆好友深夜來電

zh-tw.content:
我們這屆第一個離職的，是大學四年坐我旁邊那個。

他在群組貼了最後一天的照片，底下沒有人問為什麼，只有一整排的「恭喜」。

晚上他打來，講了四十分鐘，其中三十分鐘在說他明天終於可以睡到自然醒。

掛掉之前他反過來問我：那你呢，還撐得住嗎？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合朋友離職、或自己在猶豫的時候傳給對方，也可搭配深夜通話截圖
variations: 群組裡沒有人問他為什麼。大家都知道為什麼。
他先走了一步。而我還在原地確認自己想不想留。

en.content:
The first person from our year to quit is the one who sat next to me for four years of college.

He posted his last-day photo in the group chat, and nobody asked why — just a long row of "congrats."

He called that night and talked for forty minutes, thirty of them about finally sleeping in tomorrow.

Right before hanging up, he turned it around on me: so what about you, still holding up?
en.editorNote: For a friend who just resigned, or for the one still deciding — works with a late-night call screenshot
variations: Nobody in the chat asked why. Everybody already knew why.
He moved first. I'm still standing here deciding if I want to stay.

items.sourceNote: 職場前輩回顧自己新人時期的討論；改寫為原創的暑期實習生互動

zh-tw.content:
公司這個月來了三個暑期實習生。

其中一個要跟我借訂書機，開口叫我「哥」，我下意識回頭看後面還有沒有別人。

去年這個時候，我連影印機卡紙都要先問過人才敢碰。

沒有人通知我位置什麼時候換的，它就這樣自己換過去了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合帶到新人、或發現自己不再是最菜的那個時候發文
variations: 我還在適應被叫哥，他們已經在適應被叫新人。
菜的那一格空出來，才有人站進去。

en.content:
Three summer interns started at my company this month.

One of them asked to borrow a stapler and called me "sir" — I actually turned around to see if he meant someone behind me.

This time last year I wouldn't touch the jammed copier without asking someone first.

Nobody told me when the seat changed. It just changed.
en.editorNote: For the moment you realize you're no longer the newest person in the room
variations: I'm still adjusting to being called sir. They're adjusting to being the new ones.
Somebody has to leave the rookie chair before anybody can sit in it.

items.sourceNote: 社會新鮮人日常討論串；改寫為原創的舊筆記本場景

zh-tw.content:
開會前找不到新的空白本子，我抽了抽屜最底下那一本。

翻開才發現前面三分之一還是大三的課堂筆記，紅筆在旁邊圈了「這裡會考」。

我從中間第一頁空白開始寫今天的重點，字還是一樣醜。

同一本本子，前面在準備考試，後面在準備明天，中間沒有一頁寫著「畢業」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合翻到舊筆記、舊課本時發文，配攤開的本子或桌面照
variations: 我以為換了一種生活，結果連本子都是同一本。
課本會收起來，那個習慣寫筆記的人不會。

en.content:
Couldn't find a fresh notebook before a meeting, so I pulled the one from the bottom of the drawer.

The first third was still junior-year lecture notes, with "this will be on the test" circled in red.

I started today's notes on the first blank page in the middle. The handwriting hasn't improved.

Same notebook: the front half is studying for an exam, the back half is prepping for tomorrow, and not one page between them says "graduation."
en.editorNote: For the moment an old notebook or textbook resurfaces, paired with an open-page desk shot
variations: I thought I'd switched lives. Turns out I'm still on the same notebook.
The textbooks get boxed up. The person who takes notes doesn't.

items.sourceNote: 新鮮人求職準備資源；改寫為原創的證件照拍攝對話場景

zh-tw.content:
拍求職照那天，攝影師調完燈，轉頭問我：「可以笑一點嗎？」

我說：「可以，但不要太開心。」

她按下快門前又補一句：「放心，這種照片沒有人真的在笑。」

四年前拍學生證那張，我笑到牙齒全部露出來，那時候沒有人需要提醒我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合拍完求職照、換掉舊大頭貼那幾天發文，配新舊兩張證件照對比。
variations: 同一張臉，四年後被要求笑得剛剛好。
學生證那張笑得最醜，也最像我。

en.content:
The day I got my job headshot taken, the photographer finished with the lights and asked, "Can you smile a little?"

I said, "Sure, but not too happy."

Right before the shutter she added, "Relax, nobody in these photos is actually smiling."

In my student ID photo from four years ago I'm grinning with every tooth showing, and back then nobody had to ask.
en.editorNote: For the week you swap an old student photo for a job headshot, paired with a then-and-now portrait.
variations: Same face, four years later, now required to smile within acceptable limits.
My worst photo is still the one where I look the most like myself.

items.sourceNote: 社會新鮮人生活成本討論；改寫為原創的校園免費資源清單

zh-tw.content:
學校免費給過我三樣東西：一座沒人跟我收錢的球場、一間掛號就能去的諮商室、還有永遠找得到位子的自習區。

畢業之後這三樣各自被標上價錢：運動中心月費九百、談話一次一千八、想安靜坐兩個小時得先點一杯一百六的拿鐵。

我以為那些東西本來就長在那裡。

有人幫我付了四年，我到現在才看見那張帳單。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛畢業發現生活成本整個變樣時發文，配健身房或咖啡店收據。
variations: 四年份的免費，是有人默默結過帳的。
畢業之後才看得懂學費裡面包了什麼。

en.content:
School handed me three things for free: a court nobody charged me to use, a counseling room I could just book, and a study area that always had an open seat.

After graduation each one came with a price tag: nine hundred a month for the gym, eighteen hundred a session to talk to someone, and a hundred-sixty latte for two quiet hours at a table.

I used to think those things simply grew there.

Someone covered that bill for four years, and I'm only seeing it now.
en.editorNote: For the stretch when free campus perks turn into monthly charges, paired with a gym or coffee-shop receipt.
variations: Four years of free stuff, quietly paid for by somebody else.
You learn what tuition covered on the day it stops covering it.

items.sourceNote: 畢業後生活主題徵稿頁；改寫為原創的校園販賣機擬人視角

zh-tw.content:
我是系館一樓那台販賣機，站在樓梯轉角，第三排第二格的無糖茶最常空。

每年六月都會有一批人在我面前多站兩秒，拍完照，一枚硬幣也沒投就走了。

九月換新的人來，按同一格，罵同一句「又賣完了」。

我記不住名字，卻記得誰在期末週的半夜兩點來過，而那些人後來都沒有再回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用校園裡的老物件視角回望畢業時發文，配系館樓梯或販賣機照片。
variations: 校園裡有些東西不會畢業，它們換一批人排隊。
你走了以後，那台機器還在等下一個熬夜的人。

en.content:
I'm the vending machine on the first floor of the department building, tucked into the stairwell corner, and the unsweetened tea in row three always sells out first.

Every June a batch of people stand in front of me two seconds longer than usual, take their photo, and walk off without dropping in a single coin.

In September a new batch shows up, hits the same button, and complains the same way about it being sold out.

I don't keep names, but I remember who came by at two in the morning during finals week, and none of them ever came back.
en.editorNote: For a nostalgic post told from the point of view of something that stayed on campus, paired with a stairwell or vending-machine shot.
variations: Some things on campus never graduate; they get a new line of people instead.
After you leave, that machine keeps waiting for the next person pulling an all-nighter.

items.sourceNote: 社會新鮮人成長建議專欄；改寫為原創的緊急聯絡人欄位場景

zh-tw.content:
到職資料有一欄叫緊急聯絡人，我想都沒想就填我媽。

第二張健檢同意書，同一欄，還是我媽。

第三張表格填到一半，我的筆停住了。

大學那四年，那格我寫的都是隔壁床室友的手機，因為真的出事的那幾次，先趕到的是她。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聊室友情誼與畢業後距離時發文，配宿舍角落或表格照片。
variations: 有一段人生裡，最快趕到我身邊的不是家人。
表格換了，那個名字沒有地方可以填了。

en.content:
The onboarding packet had a line for an emergency contact, and I wrote down my mom without thinking twice.

Second form, the medical release, same line, same answer.

Halfway through the third form my pen stopped moving.

For four years of college that line always had my roommate's cell number in it, because the couple of times something actually went wrong, she was the one who got there first.
en.editorNote: For a post about roommate bonds and the distance that shows up after graduation, paired with a dorm corner or paperwork shot.
variations: There was a stretch of my life when the fastest person to reach me wasn't family.
The forms changed, and now that name has nowhere left to go.

items.sourceNote: 換日線「第一份工作：那些畢業後才知道的事」徵稿主題；改寫為原創的學生帳戶轉換場景

zh-tw.content:
銀行櫃檯前，行員把我的學生帳戶改成一般帳戶，順手在舊卡右下角剪了一個小缺口。

她問我要不要留著做紀念，我說不用，那張卡就掉進櫃檯旁邊那個透明的回收盒。

新卡兩個禮拜後寄到家裡，顏色深了一階，上面沒有校徽。

我順手翻出那本存摺，第一頁還是我爸帶我去開戶那天填的，監護人那一欄是他的字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合處理學生帳戶、換發證件這類畢業後手續時發文，配存摺或剪角舊卡照片。
variations: 卡片換了新的，第一頁的字跡沒有跟著換。
學生身分沒有告別式，只有櫃檯上那一刀。

en.content:
At the bank counter the teller flipped my student account over to a regular one and clipped a little notch out of the corner of the old card.

She asked if I wanted to keep it as a souvenir, and I said no, so it went straight into the clear recycling box beside her window.

The new card landed at my parents' place two weeks later, a shade darker, no school crest anywhere on it.

I pulled out the passbook that night, and page one is still the one my dad filled in the day he took me in to open the account, his handwriting sitting there on the guardian line.
en.editorNote: For a post about closing out student paperwork after graduation, paired with a passbook or a clipped old bank card.
variations: New card, same handwriting on page one.
Being a student doesn't get a goodbye party, just a snip at the counter.

items.sourceNote: 2026 新鮮人期望薪資調查（平均 38,315 元）；改寫為原創的首次談薪場景

zh-tw.content:
調查報告寫著，今年新鮮人的平均期望薪資是三萬八千三百一十五元。

我盯著結尾那個十五看了好久，很想知道是誰的期待被除到剩下個位數。

輪到我在面試桌上開口的時候，我報的數字比心裡想的少了三千，對面點頭點得很快。

那三千塊我讓得很順，順到走出大樓才發現自己連問都沒問一句。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合第一次談薪水、開口要價之後發文，配面試大樓或求職網頁截圖。
variations: 那個平均值裡面有一個是我，而我開口就先讓了三千。
怎麼把自己的價錢講完整，畢業前沒有人教過。

en.content:
A jobs site put out a survey saying the average new grad here is hoping for about 38,315 NT a month.

I stared at that 15 on the end for way too long, wondering whose expectations got averaged all the way down to the ones place.

When it was my turn across the interview table, I named a number three thousand lower than the one in my head, and the guy nodded fast.

I gave up that three grand so smoothly that I was already out on the sidewalk before it hit me I never asked a single question.
en.editorNote: For a post about negotiating your first salary, paired with an office lobby or a job-board screenshot.
variations: One of the numbers in that average is mine, and I discounted it before anyone asked.
Nobody teaches you how to say your own price out loud before you graduate.

items.sourceNote: 遠見「畢業後第一份工作」專題；改寫為原創的校門口街景變化

zh-tw.content:
我畢業那個月，校門口那攤賣了十幾年的滷味收了。

我搬走第二個禮拜，社辦的冷氣壞掉，學弟傳訊息來問我知不知道怎麼修。

那學期系隊沒進四強，聽說連球場的籃框都換了新的。

那條街好像跟我一起畢業了，我到現在還覺得是我害的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後回學校附近散步、發現店家換過一輪時發文，配校門口或舊招牌照片。
variations: 我一走，那條街就開始換人了。
沒有任何證據，我還是認定那些事跟我有關。

en.content:
The month I graduated, the braised-food stand that had been outside the school gate for fifteen years shut down.

Two weeks after I moved out, the AC in the club room died and a sophomore texted me asking if I knew how to fix it.

The team missed the semifinals that season, and apparently they swapped out the hoops on the court too.

That whole street graduated right along with me, and I still think it was my fault.
en.editorNote: For a post about walking past your old campus and finding half the block replaced, paired with a school gate or old signage shot.
variations: The second I left, that street started swapping people out.
No evidence whatsoever, and I'm still taking the blame for it.

items.sourceNote: 社會新鮮人職場生存建議專欄；改寫為原創的公司配發物品清單

zh-tw.content:
櫃子上那排東西都是公司給的：一台筆電、一張刷了才進得去的門禁卡、一個印著公司標誌的馬克杯、一組到現在還記不住的分機號碼，還有一個全新的自我介紹版本。

前面四樣都貼了財產編號，離職那天要一件一件還回去。

最後那樣沒有編號，是我在茶水間、電梯裡、客戶面前一句一句磨出來的。

現在有人問我是誰，我會先講公司、再講職稱，最後才輪到我從哪裡畢業。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合到職一段時間後聊身分轉換的貼文，配識別證或辦公桌一角。
variations: 公司給的東西全部都要還，講自己的那一套不用。
我的自我介紹裡，畢業那句被排到最後面了。

en.content:
Everything on that shelf came from the company: a laptop, a badge I have to tap to get through the door, a mug with the logo on it, an extension number I still can't remember, and a brand-new version of how I introduce myself.

The first four all have asset stickers on them and go back one by one the day I leave.

The last one has no sticker, since I built it a sentence at a time in the break room, in elevators, in front of clients.

These days when someone asks who I am, I lead with the company, then the title, and where I graduated from comes in dead last.
en.editorNote: For a post about the identity shift a few months into a first job, paired with a badge or a corner of your desk.
variations: Everything they hand you goes back, except the way you learned to describe yourself.
My intro still mentions my school; it just got pushed to the very end.

items.sourceNote: 換日線徵稿主題「第一份工作：那些畢業後才知道的事」的畢業後獨立生活討論，取其精神重新創作，非引用

zh-tw.content:
【第一次自己上市場．使用說明】
一、建議早上七點前抵達；八點以後，好的東西都已經在別人的籃子裡了。
二、標價牌是參考值，敢開口問的人才拿得到那個價；你第一次不敢問，很正常。
三、三把一百的青菜，一個人吃會爛掉兩把，點頭之前先算一下。
四、算錢的速度會被後面排隊的人看見，第一次慢沒關係，第二次就快了。
五、塑膠袋的提把會勒進手指，第二次記得自己帶袋子。
六、走完整排才想起忘了買蔥，這一項無法避免。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後第一次自己租屋、開始自己開伙的人發文，或傳給同期出社會、正在學著把生活撐起來的朋友
variations: 追加第七條：回家把菜攤在流理台上，你會發現份量是煮給兩個人的，那是學校留給你的習慣。
買菜這件事沒有學分，也沒有補考，第一次提著兩袋走回家就算通過。

en.content:
FIRST SOLO TRIP TO THE MARKET — PLEASE READ
1. Get there before seven. After eight, the good stuff is already in somebody else's basket.
2. The price tag is a suggestion. People who ask get a better one. You won't ask the first time, and that's fine.
3. Three bundles of greens for a hundred means two of them rot before you eat them. Do the math before you nod.
4. The people in line behind you can see how slowly you count your change. Slow is fine once; you'll be quick by the second visit.
5. The plastic handles cut into your fingers. Bring your own bag next time.
6. You will walk the whole row before remembering you forgot the scallions. This step cannot be skipped.
en.editorNote: For anyone cooking for themselves for the first time after graduating — post it, or send it to a friend learning the same things the same week
variations: Rule seven: you'll spread it all out on the counter and realize you bought for two. That's a habit school gave you.
Nobody grades grocery shopping. Getting two bags home counts as a pass.

items.sourceNote: 聯合新聞網關於畢業生處理舊課本、二手書轉手的報導，取情境重新創作，未引用原文句子

zh-tw.content:
拿去二手書店的那個紙箱，最後裝了這些：
兩本原文書，封面貼過標籤，撕掉還是留下一塊白。
一本統計課本，只有前三章有畫線。
一疊講義，右上角是別人的座號，借來影印之後忘了還。
一本社團通訊錄，最後一頁還空著沒填完。
一張當書籤用的票根，日期停在大二那年春天。
店員把票根抽出來擱在櫃台邊，說這個不算。
收了六本，退回四本，票根我放進口袋，那本書歸他們了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合搬離宿舍、清書櫃時的貼文，配一張紙箱或半空書架的照片；也適合傳給一起修過那門課的同學
variations: 書可以論斤賣，夾在書裡的那些紙沒有一個秤秤得出來。
整箱推上櫃台的時候我以為會捨不得書，結果捨不得的是一張票根。

en.content:
What ended up in the box I hauled to the used bookstore:
Two English textbooks, each with a pale patch where a sticker used to be.
One stats textbook, highlighted through chapter three and no further.
A stack of handouts with somebody else's seat number in the corner, borrowed for photocopying and never returned.
A club contact sheet with the last page still blank.
A ticket stub I'd been using as a bookmark, dated spring of sophomore year.
The clerk pulled the stub out, set it beside the register, and said that one doesn't count.
Six books in, four books back, the stub in my pocket, and the book it lived in now theirs.
en.editorNote: For clearing out a dorm shelf — pair it with a photo of the box or the half-empty bookcase, or send it to whoever took that class with you
variations: Books sell by weight. The paper tucked between them doesn't register on any scale.
I thought I'd have trouble letting go of the books. It turned out to be one ticket stub.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 工作板社會新鮮人求職迷茫討論串的氛圍，重新創作場景，非引用原文

zh-tw.content:
里民活動中心的鐵椅排成六排，前面白板上寫著今天的就業講座。

坐我前排的男生把履歷從資料夾抽出來又放回去，來回三次，最後壓在腿上用手掌把摺痕推平。

講師講到自我介紹要控制在一分鐘以內，他低頭在紙的空白處寫字，寫完又劃掉。

我坐在最後一排沒有拿筆，履歷今天已經寄出第四十一封，來這裡只是想確認還有人跟我一樣在等回音。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合投履歷投到開始懷疑自己的那個階段發文，或傳給同樣每天在刷信箱的同學
variations: 整場講座我一個字都沒記下來，只記得前排那個人把摺痕推平的手勢。
會場最安靜的那幾秒，是每個人都在等別人先舉手問問題。

en.content:
Six rows of folding chairs in the community center, a whiteboard up front with today's job workshop written on it.

The guy in the row ahead of me slid his resume out of its folder and back in, three times, then flattened the crease against his thigh with his palm.

When the speaker said to keep your self-introduction under a minute, he wrote something in the margin and crossed it out.

I sat in the back row without a pen — I sent out my forty-first application today, and I mostly came to confirm that other people are still waiting to hear back too.
en.editorNote: For the stretch of job hunting where you start doubting yourself — post it, or send it to whoever is refreshing their inbox as often as you are
variations: I didn't write down a single thing from the workshop. I remember the guy in front of me smoothing out a crease.
The quietest seconds in the room were the ones where everybody waited for somebody else to raise a hand.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 工作板「社會新鮮人工作快一年的迷茫」討論氛圍，重新創作場景與句子

zh-tw.content:
在健身房更衣室的鏡子前面，我一直在想：這樣算不算已經安定下來了？

月費綁滿一年、置物櫃的號碼背得出來、連哪一格淋浴間的熱水來得比較快都知道，這些能不能算證據？

一個人開始固定去同一個地方，會不會只是因為那裡的流程不用重新學一次？

我把濕毛巾折成四折塞進袋子，明天七點那節課已經按下預約。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業一年後、生活開始有固定形狀時的貼文，配一張運動包、置物櫃鑰匙或深夜的健身房走廊
variations: 安定的證據沒有想像中偉大，可能只是知道哪一格淋浴間的熱水來得比較快。
問題都還沒有答案，但明天七點的位置我已經先卡好了。

en.content:
In front of the gym locker room mirror I keep asking: does this count as settled?

A membership locked in for a year, a locker number I know by heart, the one shower stall that heats up fastest — do those count as evidence?

Or does going to the same place on a fixed schedule just mean it's the one routine I don't have to learn from scratch?

I fold the wet towel into quarters, push it into my bag, and book tomorrow's seven o'clock class.
en.editorNote: For the point a year out of school where life starts having a fixed shape — pair it with a gym bag, a locker key, or an empty late-night hallway
variations: The evidence for a settled life is smaller than expected: knowing which shower stall heats up fastest.
None of the questions have answers yet, but tomorrow's seven o'clock slot is already mine.

items.sourceNote: 自備環保杯至少折 5 元的手搖飲政策報導，取其消費明細情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
【取餐口　09 號　感謝惠顧】
大杯紅茶拿鐵　微糖少冰　65
自備環保杯　－5
學生證優惠　本月起失效
「老樣子」這三個字　用了四年　0
實付　60　付款方式　打工最後一筆尾款
店員在封膜上寫：畢業快樂，記得回來喝
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後最後一次去常喝的那家手搖店，配一張封膜、號碼牌或杯子上的手寫字
variations: 學生證折扣會失效，但「老樣子」這三個字他們記了四年。
最貴的那一杯不在價目表上，是最後一次能理直氣壯說老樣子的那杯。

en.content:
[PICKUP WINDOW 09 — THANK YOU]
Large black tea latte, less sugar, less ice — 65
Brought my own cup — 5 off
Student discount — expired this month
Saying "the usual" for four years — 0
Total 60, paid with the last of my part-time money
Written on the seal by the clerk: congrats, come back thirsty
en.editorNote: For the last run to the drink shop you lived at — pair it with the sealed lid, the order number, or the handwriting on the cup
variations: The student discount expires. The fact that they still remember "the usual" doesn't.
The most expensive cup isn't on the menu — it's the last one you get to order without explaining.

items.sourceNote: 退租點交與押金扣款流程說明，取其明細表形式重新創作畢業搬離場景，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
【押金退還明細　4B　最後一天】
押金　一萬五
牆上便利貼留下的膠痕　－300
紗窗破洞　搬進來就有，房東記得　0
冷氣濾網　走之前自己洗過兩次　0
門框上量身高的鉛筆記號　沒有人提起
實退　一萬四千七，房東又多塞兩百說當紅包
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合搬離念書時租的房子那天，配一張空房間、鑰匙或門框鉛筆記號的照片
variations: 押金退了一萬四千七，門框上那些鉛筆記號他們沒有算錢。
房東多塞的那兩百塊，是這間房子最後一次跟我說話。

en.content:
[DEPOSIT RETURN — UNIT 4B, FINAL DAY]
Deposit — 15,000
Glue marks from sticky notes on the wall — 300
Torn window screen (already there, landlord remembers) — 0
AC filter (washed it twice before leaving) — 0
Pencil height marks on the door frame — nobody brings them up
Returned: 14,700, plus 200 he pressed into my hand as a gift
en.editorNote: For moving out of the place you rented through school — pair it with the emptied room, the keys, or the pencil marks on the door frame
variations: They deducted for the sticky-note glue and charged nothing for the pencil marks on the door frame.
That extra 200 he pushed back at me was the apartment's way of saying goodbye.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 工作板新鮮人求職與面試準備討論氛圍，重新創作為理髮對話，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
「要剪多短？」
「短到面試官看不出來我上禮拜還在趕報告。」
「瀏海呢？」
「留一點，我媽說看起來比較有精神。」
「染回黑色嗎？」
「嗯，先黑一年，看看之後還有沒有機會亂來。」
「洗完幫你吹直？」
「不用，我想記得它本來捲成什麼樣子。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合面試前把頭髮剪短、染回黑色那天發，配一張剪完的鏡子自拍或地上的頭髮
variations: 先黑一年，剩下的顏色我幫它記著。
頭髮可以剪短，但我要記得它本來捲成什麼樣子。

en.content:
"How short?"
"Short enough that no one can tell I was still writing papers last week."
"And the bangs?"
"Leave some. My mom says it makes me look awake."
"Dyeing it back to black?"
"Yeah. Black for a year, then we'll see if I still get to mess around."
"Blow it straight after the wash?"
"Nah. I want to remember how it curled on its own."
en.editorNote: For the pre-interview haircut, the day you go back to black — pair it with a mirror selfie or the hair on the salon floor
variations: Black for a year. I'll keep the other colors on file.
Cut it as short as you want — I just want to remember how it curled on its own.

items.sourceNote: 大學畢業季清運無主單車、開放認養的新聞，取其情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
「這台還騎嗎？不騎的話學校要清掉喔。」

腳踏車棚最裡面那一格，坐墊曬到褪色，鎖孔卡了三年份的灰。輪胎沒氣，鈴鐺按下去剩一聲悶悶的鈍響，後架上的系隊貼紙翹了一半。我把鑰匙轉了兩下，鎖開了，車還是我的，但我已經沒有理由每天七點半把它牽出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後回學校牽車、處理留在校園裡的東西時發，配一張腳踏車棚或褪色坐墊的照片
variations: 鑰匙還轉得開，我卻沒有理由每天七點半把它牽出來了。
車還是我的，缺的是那個非騎不可的早上。

en.content:
"You still riding this one? If not, the school's hauling it off."

Last slot at the back of the bike shed: seat bleached pale, three years of dust packed into the lock. Flat tire, a bell that manages one dull thud, half the team sticker peeling off the rear rack. I turn the key twice and it opens — still my bike, though I no longer have a reason to wheel it out at seven thirty every morning.
en.editorNote: For going back to campus to collect what you left there — pair it with the bike shed or a sun-bleached seat
variations: The key still turns. The seven-thirty reason for turning it is gone.
It's still my bike. What's missing is the morning that needed it.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 討論串「畢業以後跟大部分同學失聯正常嗎」的網友回應，取其情緒重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
【畢業滿一年．河堤步道自我測驗】
問：跑到第三座橋墩，你才想起今天是誰的生日。你會怎麼做？
（A）打開班群發一張貼圖，等別人先接話
（B）點進他的限時動態，看完，什麼都沒按
（C）傳一句「生日快樂」，後面補一個有點心虛的表情
（D）耳機音量調大，繼續往前跑，跑到堤防盡頭再說
（E）停下來，回撥那通去年沒接完的電話　←　被原子筆圈了兩圈
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業一年後在河堤慢跑、突然想起老同學的那種心情，配一張黃昏堤防或跑鞋的照片
variations: 跑到第三座橋墩才想起來，又跑了兩公里才決定要按下去。
去年沒接完的那通電話，我今年在河堤上補撥了回去。

en.content:
[One Year Out — Riverside Trail Self-Assessment]
Q: You reach the third bridge pillar before you remember whose birthday it is. You:
(A) Drop a sticker in the class group chat and wait for someone else to go first
(B) Open his story, watch all of it, tap nothing
(C) Send "happy birthday" with an emoji that comes out a little sheepish
(D) Turn the music up and keep running to the end of the levee
(E) Stop, and call back the one you let ring last year  ← circled twice in ballpoint
en.editorNote: For that jolt on a riverside run a year after graduating, when an old classmate surfaces out of nowhere — pair it with dusk on the levee or your running shoes
variations: Remembered at the third pillar, ran two more kilometers before deciding to press call.
The call I let ring last year, I returned this year, on the riverbank.

items.sourceNote: 2026 職場新鮮人調查（76% 計畫投入職場）新聞，取其「畢業後赴外地報到」情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
登機門的廣播正在第三次念她的名字，她還在跟她媽講電話，講的是落地以後要不要先吃飯這種小事。

隊伍縮到剩五個人，她把行李箱的拉桿收起來又拉出來，收起來又拉出來。她背包側袋插著一張捲起來的紙，畢業證書，說是報到那天要用。

輪到她了，她把手機從耳邊放下，說「我到了再打給你」，然後把登機證翻成正面。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送機那天、或自己飛去外地報到時發，配一張登機門排隊或停機坪的照片
variations: 拉桿收起來又拉出來，她只是想再多站三十秒。
背包側袋那張捲起來的紙，比行李箱裡任何一件衣服都重要。

en.content:
The gate is calling her name for the third time and she's still on the phone with her mom, working out whether to eat before or after she lands.

The line is down to five people and she keeps collapsing her suitcase handle and pulling it back out, collapsing it and pulling it back out. There's a rolled-up sheet of paper in the side pocket of her backpack — the diploma, for her first day.

Her turn: she takes the phone from her ear, says "I'll call you when I'm there," and flips the boarding pass right side up.
en.editorNote: For the day you see someone off, or fly out yourself to start somewhere new — pair it with the boarding line or the tarmac
variations: The handle goes down and comes back up. She just wants thirty more seconds of standing still.
That rolled-up sheet in the side pocket outranks everything in the suitcase.

items.sourceNote: 台灣社會新鮮人第一份工作停留時間的報導，取其職涯抉擇主題重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
如果那年我沒有把履歷投出去，現在應該就站在這塊鐵板前面，用油爆的聲音判斷蛋要翻面了沒。

如果我真的接了家裡這攤，我會記得哪個客人不要美乃滋、哪個客人的鐵板麵永遠多加一顆蛋；我現在記得的，是一整排叫不出臉的職稱。如果我留下來，大概也會在某個下雨的早上，站在同一個位置想另一個沒發生的版本。

老闆娘正把蛋翻過來，我的火腿蛋吐司還有一分鐘，她認得我，只是不知道我剛剛想了這麼遠。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回老家吃早餐、想起自己曾經有另一種人生選項的時候發，配一張鐵板或吐司袋的照片
variations: 油爆的聲音我到現在還聽得懂，只是這幾年沒有機會用到。
另一個版本的我在翻蛋，這個版本的我在等蛋。

en.content:
If I hadn't sent that résumé out, I'd be standing at this griddle right now, telling by the crackle of the oil when the egg needs turning.

If I'd taken over the family stand, I'd know which customer skips the mayo and which one always wants an extra egg on the noodles; what I know instead is a wall of job titles I can't attach to faces. If I'd stayed, I'd probably still be here on some rainy morning, in this exact spot, running the other version that never happened.

The owner flips the egg, my ham-and-egg toast is a minute out, and she knows my face — she just doesn't know how far I got in my head.
en.editorNote: For breakfast back in your hometown, when the life you didn't pick is standing right in front of you — pair it with the griddle or a paper toast bag
variations: I can still read the crackle of the oil. I just haven't needed to in years.
One version of me flips the egg. This version waits for it.

items.sourceNote: Mobile01「2026 剛出社會必看」求職討論串，取其新鮮人長時間盯螢幕的生活細節重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
驗光師把新的度數念出來，我才知道這幾年一共加深了兩百度。

上一副是去年配的，那時剛進公司，天天盯著兩個螢幕改簡報，改到眼睛乾得要用手撐開。再上一副是大四那年，論文最後一個月，圖書館放閉館音樂我才捨得抬頭。

最早那一副，是高三某天午睡醒來，黑板上的字忽然糊成一片，我媽帶我來的就是這間店，坐的就是這張椅子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合換眼鏡、驗完光走出店門那天發，配一張驗光儀或新鏡框的照片
variations: 度數是一份沒人幫你寫的資歷，你看過的每個螢幕它都記得。
同一間店、同一張椅子，換掉的只有陪我來的那個人。

en.content:
The optometrist reads out the new numbers, and that's how I find out I've picked up two more diopters in a few years.

The last pair was from last year, my first months on the job, two monitors and slides rewritten until my eyes went dry enough to need propping open. The pair before that was senior year, the final month of my thesis, the library's closing music the only thing that ever got my head up.

The first pair came from a nap in high school — I woke to a blackboard gone soft at the edges, and my mom walked me into this same shop, to this same chair.
en.editorNote: For the day you pick up new glasses and step back out onto the street — pair it with the phoropter or a fresh pair of frames
variations: Your prescription is a résumé nobody helped you write. Every screen you ever stared at is on it.
Same shop, same chair. The only thing swapped out is who came with me.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 心情板「現下年輕人去KTV都在唱什麼」討論串的點歌氛圍，重新創作為畢業季續攤場景，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
整晚我都負責點歌、幫別人卡調、遞衛生紙給哭到妝花掉的人，一邊跟自己說，沒哭就不算捨不得。

謝師宴散場之後我們續攤到凌晨，我切掉三首太芭樂的歌，還笑說這種場合唱這個很老套。直到螢幕右上角跳出紅色的「本包廂剩餘 05 分」，有人把麥克風塞進我手裡，我才發現自己抖到握不穩。

那五分鐘我一句都沒唱，只是坐著把整首聽完，然後在心裡承認：我從三個小時前就捨不得了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合謝師宴續攤那一晚，或畢業季最後一次跟同學唱歌時發，配一張點歌螢幕或桌上麥克風的照片
variations: 我切掉了三首歌，最後還是坐著把那一首整個聽完。
螢幕跳出剩五分鐘的那一刻，我才肯承認自己捨不得。

en.content:
All night I worked the song queue, fixed everyone's key, passed tissues to whoever's makeup had run — telling myself that as long as I didn't cry, none of this was getting to me.

We kept the room going past midnight after the dinner, and I skipped three songs for being too sappy, laughing that nobody picks those anymore. Then red text showed up in the corner of the screen — ROOM TIME REMAINING 05:00 — someone pushed the mic into my hand, and I couldn't hold it steady.

I didn't sing a word of those five minutes. I sat there and listened to the whole song, and admitted to myself that it had been getting to me for three hours already.
en.editorNote: For the after-party that runs past midnight at the end of graduation season — pair it with the song queue screen or a mic left on the table
variations: I skipped three songs and still sat through every second of the last one.
It took a red 05:00 in the corner of the screen before I'd admit I wasn't ready to leave.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 心情板「離家前的心情調適」討論串，取其離家前一晚的家庭情緒重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
「碗放著，我來洗就好。」

「你明天六點的車，早點去睡。」

我的手還泡在水裡，沒有拿起來，也沒有講出真正的理由：我只是想在這個位置多站十分鐘。再過一個禮拜，我要洗的就會是租屋處那個小到放不下湯鍋的不鏽鋼槽，而她要一個人洗兩人份的碗。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合離家去外地上班的前一晚發，配一張水槽、瀝水籃或家裡那組舊碗的照片
variations: 那十分鐘我洗得特別慢，慢到水都涼了。
她說早點睡，我聽成的卻是下次不知道什麼時候再一起洗碗。

en.content:
"Leave the dishes. I've got them."

"Your bus is at six. Go to bed."

I kept my hands in the water and didn't give her the real reason: I just wanted ten more minutes standing in that exact spot. A week from now the sink I wash in will be the dorm-sized steel basin that can't fit a soup pot, and she'll be doing two people's dishes by herself.
en.editorNote: For the night before you leave home for a job in another city — pair it with the sink, the drying rack, or the bowls you grew up eating from
variations: I washed slowly enough that the water went cold.
She said go to bed. What I heard was: no telling when we'll do dishes together again.

items.sourceNote: 臺大保健中心校園捐血車活動頁（時間、地點、捐血條件），取其校園捐血情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
第一次是大一，被室友拖上車，為了那條印著校徽的毛巾，護理師說手要握緊，我緊張到把拳頭握出汗。

第二次是大三，系上辦活動缺人數，我躺在那張窄窄的躺椅上盯著天花板，十分鐘就結束，下車還順手拿了兩包餅乾。

第三次是上個月，車停在公司對面，沒有人揪我。表格上的職業欄我停了三秒，才把公司名字寫下去——前面兩次，那一欄我都寫學生。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後第一次以上班族的身分，做以前學生時代做過的事，配一張捐血車或手臂上那塊膠布的照片
variations: 同一張表格填第三次，只有職業那一欄換了字。
前兩次都是被人揪去的，第三次是我自己走上車的。

en.content:
The first time was freshman year: my roommate dragged me on board for the towel with the school crest, the nurse told me to keep my fist closed, and I squeezed it sweaty.

The second time was junior year, when my department needed bodies for a service event. I lay on that narrow chair staring at the ceiling, it was over in ten minutes, and I grabbed two packs of crackers on my way out.

The third time was last month. The van was parked across from my office and nobody talked me into it. On the form I stalled three seconds at the occupation line before writing my company's name — the first two times, that line just said student.
en.editorNote: For the first time you do a student-era thing and answer as a working adult — pair it with the donation van or the tape on your arm
variations: Same form, third round. Only the occupation line came out different.
The first two times somebody dragged me there. The third time I walked on by myself.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 心情板「為什麼大家大學畢業就不怎麼 po IG 限動了」討論串，取其畢業後社群互動的變化重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
畢業那天的大合照，我以為自己沒有被叫到，這個誤會擺了兩年。

限時動態上的那張是正方形版本，左右各切掉一截，我在裡面怎麼找都找不到自己。上個月有人翻出硬碟裡的原檔丟進群組，說要洗成相片本，我點開放大，最右邊那個舉著手、只剩半個身體的人就是我。

原來我一直都站在裡面，只是站在大家看到的那個畫面外。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合翻到舊照片原檔、發現自己記錯了某件事的時候發，配一張大合照或未裁切原圖的照片
variations: 被切掉的是畫面的邊緣，我一直都在那裡舉著手。
一個誤會可以擺兩年，拆穿它只需要放大一次。

en.content:
For two years I believed nobody called me over for the class photo on graduation day.

The version I'd seen was the square crop from someone's story, a slice gone off each side, and no matter how long I looked I couldn't find myself in it. Last month someone dug the original off an old hard drive and dropped it in the group chat to get prints made — I zoomed in, and the person on the far right with a hand up, half of him cut off, was me.

I'd been standing there the whole time. I was just outside the frame everyone happened to be looking at.
en.editorNote: For the moment an old file proves your memory wrong — pair it with the class photo or the uncropped original
variations: The edges got cropped. I was in that shot the entire time.
A misunderstanding can sit for two years and take one zoom to undo.

items.sourceNote: TVBS 報導校園「司令台」名稱爭議與各校改名為集會台／升旗台，取其「同一座台子看過幾十屆學生」的視角重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
我是操場司令台，一整塊水泥灌出來的，六月的太陽把我曬到能煎蛋，六百多個孩子在我面前坐成方陣。

校長站上來講了四十分鐘，三十七年份的祝福我早就會背，連他在哪個逗點吸氣都知道。

真正留在我身上的是散場之後：兩個女生爬上來，把便當盒墊在腳邊，看著空掉的球場一直不走。

她們坐到天黑，那是我一整年裡唯一一次覺得自己不是拿來讓人抬頭看的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業典禮當天或回母校時發，配一張空掉的操場、或典禮結束後沒人的台階照片
variations: 被人抬頭看了三十七年，最記得的卻是有人願意坐下來的那個傍晚。
台上講的那些我全都會背了，台下沒說的那些我才記得住。

en.content:
I am the concrete assembly platform at the head of the field, hot enough by June to fry an egg, with six hundred kids sitting in rows in front of me.

The principal climbs up and talks for forty minutes, and I have thirty-seven years of the same blessing memorised, right down to which comma he breathes at.

What actually stays with me is what happens after everyone leaves: two girls climbed up, set their lunch boxes down by their feet, and looked out at the emptied field without going anywhere.

They sat there until dark, and that was the one hour all year I didn't feel like something built to be looked up at.
en.editorNote: For graduation day itself or a visit back to campus — pair it with an empty field or the bare steps after the ceremony
variations: Thirty-seven years of being looked up at, and what I remember is the evening someone sat down.
I know every word said from up here. It's the words said down there that stayed.

items.sourceNote: 自由評論網投書〈別再「司令台」了！〉談各校把司令台改名為建中台、中女台等，取其「舊字牌被換下」的物件視角重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
掛了四十年，他們終於把我從水泥牆面上拆下來，換上三個新字：集會台。

拆我的那天離畢業典禮只剩一個禮拜，工人把我靠在操場司令台側邊，我這輩子頭一次用側躺的角度看整片球場。

典禮那天唸到某個名字，後排突然爆出一陣笑，那孩子衝上台的腳步聲穿過水泥，敲在我背面。

牆上的字換了，我背了四十年的那些名字沒有換。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合母校改建、老建築拆掉、或畢業後看到學校變樣的時候發，配舊校舍或施工圍籬的照片
variations: 他們換掉了我的名字，沒換掉我記得的那些名字。
被拆下來的那天我才發現，我這四十年真正掛著的地方，是底下站過的那幾千個人。

en.content:
After forty years on that wall they finally pried me off and put up three new characters in my place.

They took me down a week before the ceremony, and the workmen leaned me against the side of the platform, so for the first time in my life I saw the whole field lying on my side.

On the day itself a name got read out and the back rows burst out laughing, and I felt that kid's footsteps come pounding up through the concrete into my back.

The words on the wall got replaced. The names I've been carrying for forty years did not.
en.editorNote: For when your old school gets rebuilt or a familiar building comes down — pair it with the old campus or the construction hoarding
variations: They swapped out my name. They couldn't swap out the ones I remember.
The day they pried me off, I found out what I had actually been hanging on for forty years: the few thousand people who stood underneath me.

items.sourceNote: 輔仁大學畢業服歸還與畢業證書領取公告（逾期須賠償、可掛號寄回），取其「租來的袍子被還回去」的物件視角重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
我這件袍子被穿過十一年，每年六月出門一趟，七月回到同一個衣櫥裡，肩線比剛出廠時鬆了兩指寬。

今年那個女生把我穿得特別久，典禮散了三小時還不肯脫，拖著我走過操場、走過司令台的水泥階，帽穗一路掃我的領口。

歸還那天，她在袋子裡塞了字條，說謝謝我陪她走完這一趟，收袍子的阿姨笑說衣服又不識字。

她不知道，我肩上那幾根鬆掉的線記得每一個抱過她的人用了多大力氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合歸還學士服、把租來的東西還掉、或收拾畢業當天衣物的時候發，配袍子摺好裝袋的照片
variations: 我身上沒有一個字是你的，可是我肩上的線全是你的。
衣服要還回去，被抱過的力氣還不回去。

en.content:
This gown has been worn by eleven different people, one trip out every June and back into the same wardrobe by July, the shoulders two fingers looser than the day I was made.

This year's girl kept me on far longer than the rest, still wearing me three hours after it ended, dragging me across the field and up the concrete steps of the platform with her tassel brushing my collar the whole way.

When she handed me back there was a note tucked in the bag thanking me for walking it with her, and the woman collecting gowns laughed and said clothes can't read.

What she doesn't know is that the loose threads at my shoulder remember exactly how hard every single person hugged her.
en.editorNote: For returning a rented gown or packing away graduation-day clothes — pair it with the folded gown in its bag
variations: Not one word on me belongs to you. Every loose thread does.
The gown goes back. The hugs it took don't.

items.sourceNote: VoiceTube 部落格介紹各國畢業傳統與撥穗（turning of the tassel）流蘇由右撥到左的儀式，取其「流蘇本人」的物件視角重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
他們叫我流蘇，我的一生只有兩秒鐘的工作：從右邊被撥到左邊。

那兩秒之前，我在他頭上晃了整個上午，晃過大合照、晃過司令台的階梯、晃過他假裝揉眼睛的那一下。

那兩秒之後，我被塞進背包，壓在筆電和半包餅乾中間，一路晃回租屋處。

現在我掛在他書桌檯燈的支架上，看他一封一封投履歷；他大概忘了，我這條線生下來就是用來標記「換邊」這件事的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合畢業後在找工作、覺得儀式感一下就過去了的時候發，配學士帽或流蘇被隨手掛著的照片
variations: 整場典禮我只被需要兩秒，剩下的日子我都在旁邊看他慢慢換邊。
撥過去只要兩秒，走過去要幾年。

en.content:
They call me a tassel, and my entire life's work lasts two seconds: getting flipped from the right side to the left.

For the whole morning before those two seconds I swung above his head, through the group photo, up the steps of the assembly platform, through the moment he pretended he was rubbing his eye.

For the hours after them I was crammed into a backpack between a laptop and half a packet of biscuits, swinging all the way back to his rented room.

Now I hang off the arm of his desk lamp watching him send out application after application, and I don't think he remembers that marking the switch from one side to the other is the only thing I was ever made to do.
en.editorNote: For job-hunting season after graduation, when the ceremony already feels far away — pair it with a cap or tassel left hanging somewhere
variations: Two seconds is all anyone needed me for. I've spent every day since watching him make the same switch slowly.
Flipping it takes two seconds. Becoming it takes years.

items.sourceNote: 臺大計資中心介紹校內「校園公布欄」線上系統（489 個單位使用、上線以來累積近五萬則、以電子化取代紙本），取其「紙本板面被換掉」的對照重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
系館走廊那面公布欄，左邊數來第三格是我大一搶下來的位置，社團招生海報用四顆圖釘固定，右下角是我用奇異筆補上去的手機號碼。

上個月回學校，那一格擺著研究所的海報，紙很新，四個角壓得很平。

我伸手摸左上角，圖釘留下的四個洞還在，指腹按下去會陷進去一點點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合回母校、經過以前貼過東西的那塊板子時發，配公布欄近拍或圖釘孔的照片
variations: 海報換過三輪，那四個洞的位置沒有人補過。
我搶下來的是一格板面，留下來的是四個洞。

en.content:
On the board in the hallway outside my department, the third slot from the left was the one I grabbed as a freshman: a club recruitment poster held down with four pins, my phone number added at the bottom right in marker.

I went back to campus last month. That slot holds a grad school poster now, new paper, all four corners lying flat.

I reached up and touched the top left corner. The four pinholes are still there, and my fingertip still sinks in.
en.editorNote: For a visit back to campus and the board you once claimed a corner of — pair it with a close-up of the board or the pinholes
variations: Three rounds of posters later, nobody has filled in those four holes.
What I fought for was a slot on a board. What stayed was four holes.

items.sourceNote: 清華大學生活輔導組失物招領頁（拾獲物品登記、保管方式與招領流程），取其「掉的東西被列在板面上等人來認」的情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
高一把外套丟在球場那次，隔天在公布欄上看到一張紅筆寫的紙，上頭列著一支雨傘、一個便當袋，還有一件深藍色連帽外套。

上禮拜整理房間，那件外套從衣櫃最底下翻出來，袖口磨白了兩塊，拉鍊卡在一半上不去。

我把它掛回去，這次沒有人會替我寫那張紙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合翻出學生時代舊衣服、或搬家整理到一半停下來的時候發，配舊外套或磨白袖口的照片
variations: 紅筆寫的那張紙救回它一次，後來是我自己從衣櫃底下撈出來的。
袖口那兩塊白，是它跟我一起走到這裡的證據。

en.content:
The time I left my jacket on the court in tenth grade, there was a sheet up the next day in red pen listing an umbrella, a lunch bag, and one navy hooded jacket.

I cleaned out my room last week and that jacket came up from the bottom of the wardrobe, two patches worn white at the cuffs, the zip stuck halfway.

I hung it back up. This time nobody is going to write that sheet for me.
en.editorNote: For unearthing a piece of school-era clothing mid-clean-out — pair it with the old jacket or its worn cuffs
variations: A sheet in red pen got it back once. After that it was just me, digging at the bottom of a wardrobe.
The two white patches at the cuffs are how far it came with me.

items.sourceNote: 長榮大學課外活動組海報張貼申請規定（全校七個貼點、每點限一張、以圖釘或無痕膠帶固定、十四天後須自行撤除），取其「跑遍全校貼海報」的情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
大二辦成發，全校七個貼點我騎腳踏車繞了一整個下午，每張海報四個角各壓一顆圖釘，十四天到了得自己回去撕。

宿舍區那塊公布欄我蓋到了別人的紙，被學長叫住講了三分鐘。

上個月公司走廊換了新的軟木板，我印的那張活動單獨佔一整面，四個角我照樣壓了圖釘，沒有人來跟我搶。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合出社會後看到公司佈告板、想起學生時代搶版面那段日子時發，配軟木板或一把圖釘的照片
variations: 七個貼點跑一個下午，換成一整面板子沒人跟我搶。
壓圖釘的手勢沒變，會來罵我的那個人不在了。

en.content:
Sophomore year I biked to all seven posting spots on campus in one afternoon for our department showcase, a pin in each corner of every poster, and in fourteen days I had to go take them all down myself.

On the board in the dorm area I covered part of somebody else's flyer, and an upperclassman stopped me for a three-minute talk about it.

Last month the office hallway got a new corkboard. The one thing I printed has the whole surface to itself, I still put a pin in each corner, and nobody comes to fight me for the space.
en.editorNote: For the moment an office corkboard reminds you of fighting for wall space on campus — pair it with a board or a handful of pins
variations: An afternoon for seven spots then. A whole board to myself now.
Same pin, same four corners. Nobody left to tell me off.

items.sourceNote: 政治大學課外活動組海報張貼管理系統（校內海報版位線上申請與管理），取其「板面上那張自己貼的小紙條」情境重新創作，內容全新

zh-tw.content:
大一在系館一樓的公布欄貼過一張家教紙條，下緣剪成十二條，每條印著同一組電話。

一個禮拜被撕走七條，我每天下課都繞過去數一次，剩五條那天還特地退後兩步看。

那塊板子去年換成有玻璃門的，裡頭乾乾淨淨；我電話沒換過，那五條大概還夾在誰的錢包裡，或者早就被揉掉了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看到舊式公布欄、或想起學生時代自己接的第一份工作時發，配剪成一條一條的紙條照片
variations: 剪了十二條，被撕走七條，另外五條的下落我一直沒查到。
電話號碼沒換，願意伸手撕一條走的人換了好幾輪。

en.content:
Freshman year I put a tutoring flyer on the board on the ground floor of my department building, the bottom edge cut into twelve tabs, the same phone number on every one.

Seven tabs were gone within a week. I detoured past it after class every day to count, and on the day it was down to five I stepped back to look at it.

They swapped that board for one with a glass door last year, and it's spotless in there. My number never changed. Those five tabs are probably still folded in somebody's wallet, or they got balled up years ago.
en.editorNote: For spotting an old-style bulletin board, or remembering the little hustle you ran as a student — pair it with a flyer cut into pull tabs
variations: Twelve tabs cut, seven taken, five I never traced.
The number stayed the same. The people willing to tear one off did not.
